Story line is a strait forward linear, you can do some exploration around levels to go for hidden rewards and such(Listening to the guy explain each one is quite interesting and due to actor brilliant voice cast amusing), the emotions done in the game and the very own powers messing with your mind it can be a real challange to sometimes go along with some of the "do that or don't do it" situations in the game, for that part it is good that story is linear because otherwise game wouldn't make any sense what so ever.
Graphics are not really top notch but they still do add a shade of its own style to liven up(or beat down) the atmosphere of the story.
Multiplayer I did not play more then 5-10 minutes so I can't give any solid date but it seemed promising minus the annoying fact about light(I'll get on that later), for as much I've seen it seems to be an add-on to the story it self, "cleaning up" behind what you did in story line[or make more mess(usualy the latter)] so it's a Co-Op, don't believe there is a PvP aspect of the multiplayer even thou I've checked.
There aren't many bugs, as fact I've only encounterd a small annoying thing(mentioned earlier), and that is that being in the or under light is impossible to play, screen is too white to do anything even on minimum gamma.
There is where I wish they added some kind of "off/on" button or toggle, since it is in entire story line that you fight the "Darkness", heck in the intro your character has constrained it near completly, and I loved the part <SPOILER> where you're are striped of your powers, I was just standing under a floodlight for about bit more then 5 minutes just enjoying my self (then I shot the generator out of habit and went about kicking some more♥♥♥♥♥.
If that was an added option that would give an very good edge(probably make the player too overpowerd, but thats what the Hard difficulty is for anyway).
Graphics: Don't give me much awe but they've made them good enough to go with the mood of story.
Story: I have to admit, this is one of those games that hit the 100 point center, twice. Ending <3
Gameplay: Well the AI is pretty well done, players skills interact well, and boss fights are fun and the game world has that "mafia" touch baked just right.
Overall 81/100

One of the most unremarkable games I have ever played. Very generic. A 4/10 at best. The stealth mechanics are non-existent: you can crouch and sneak, but enemies can hear you or see you or spot you in disguise too easily because their cones of vision are programmed very sloppily. Technically, the game feels very unfinished, because it is. Enemy cones of vision are broken: sometimes they cannot see me when I am crouching in a slight shadow right in front of them in a well lit area, other times they can spot me when they shouldn't be able to, like for instance seeing me in disguise through a wall. The graphics suck balls and the sound is instantly forgettable. The gameplay has a very generic game feel and the controls are very loose and generic.
However I was playing through it for quite a while and there is one massive fundamental flaw that had me uninstalling this, never to be played again: a horrific checkpoint system. You can be spotted by guards very easily and end up dying or encounter a game bug like I did and will sometimes have to replay a massive chunk of the level which is unacceptable by todays standards. Having to replay such large parts in such a bland game is extra torture. I was entertaining the possibility of trudging through it and beating the whole game until the final nail was hammered into the coffin. In the level where you go through the trainyard and have to plant explosives on the train, I planted the explosives, watched it blow up, and then discovered I was stuck there because unbeknownst to me because the game has a total lack of direction, I was, I think, supposed to climb back up where I had come before the few seconds it took before the bomb went off. That's the only thing I can think of because I was stuck and could not progress anymore. The final nail came when I selected "load checkpoint" because I had no other choice and it put me way, way back, and I would have had to replay a massive section of the level.
If a great game that is a proper stealth game (in which this game is unmistakably not one) like Splinter Cell or the new Thief game or even Dishonored, had only a decent checkpointing system, that would be sort of okay. This game is a double threat because not only does it suck bad, the checkpointing system isn't even decent, it totally sucks.
This game is a 4/10 at best and that is being very generous.

The masterpiece that defined a genre.
DOOM truly is a masterclass in game design, and it has kept me coming back for over 20 years.
The unmodified version that Steam provides is awful and runs through DOSbox, so if you plan on buying DOOM I highly recommend playing it with the "GZDoom" source port for some much needed quality of life changes. This will mean copying the WAD files to the extracted "GZDoom" file folder and running the game from the "GZDoom" exe on the desktop. As a result, you will never be launching the game through Steam, so don't expect it to track your playtime hours.
***Final Note: Don't buy into what people are saying about the DOOM 2016 game being "just like the original". From a game design standpoint, DOOM 1993 and DOOM 2016 differ to the extreme and effectively fall into different FPS genres.  If you want the advertised "classic FPS gameplay", DOOM 2016 (while still a competent shooter) is a♥♥♥♥♥♥poor substitute for the original.

My favourite game of 11 years. (spoilers below)
Pros:
- Brilliant storyline (not as good as the first, but still had be completely absorbed).
- The world is incredible, visiting Peragus and Telos just to get your ship back, seeing the aftermath of the events in KotOR on Korriban and Dantooine, visiting new planets mentioned in the movies like Onderon, Dxun and Nar Shaddaa and going to extra areas only accessed later, like the Ravager and Malachor.
- Character progression is (in my opinion) way better than the first in terms of powers and feats, made even better by a couple of mods, including the prestige system which makes you completely overpowered if optimised right.
- Companions are all more than worth talking to, offering story, lore, opinions and insights and even benefitting you in ways such as abilities and increasing your power. Also the ability to turn them into Jedi once you've been with them enough is incredibly beneficial.
- So many items! And a ton of craftable upgrades to each, each piece offering certain advantages and disadvantages.
- You can be a♥♥♥♥♥♥to literally everyone and not care about a single thing (including being called a "delightfully random cruelty generator" while "poisoning all you touch with your presence") it's honestly surprising your companions stay with you with unneccasary death threats whenever they cough.
Cons
- You can lose your family to the game.
- You can tell the game wasn't finished before release with a couple of parts, which is a damned shame, but has been addressed (sorta) in a mod.

Update 1-10-2017. Been doing quite some PvP lately since pve was basically mastered. And it completely ruined the game for me. Expect hours and hours of frustration. Expect being matched vs people that exploit everything they can. Expect being matched vs people much more experienced then you and it completely ruins the game. There is no fun in pvp whatsoever, it is based on abusing the exploits. Thanks to this, I'm pretty much done with PvP in this game, and since pve hasn't all that much appeal anymore after a while, this game is another gem that could be great, but is ultimately destroyed by the community that plays it and the devs that don't listen.
I was looking out for this game thanks to the trailers. Truth be told, I was expecting a different game. A single player game I guess.
I was pleasantly welcomed by doing the story, which is great. It's challenging and it looks awesome. Other then that I also loved the story on its own
However I soon discovered that once you finish the story, all that's left is multiplayer. And the Story is on the short side, so I was dissapointed as PvP isn't my thing.
Then I gave it a shot and boy, do I love this game. I rarely do Pvp, but that's ok as you can do EVERYTHING as co op instead. And that's something I absolutely love. 1v1, 2v2, 4v4, point capture. All humans vs the AI. YES!
So with playability after story covered, it was time to look into the different heroes. And different they are! You have 3 "races" and each has 4 classes. Each one is unique. So that means you have plenty of choice (12) to find a hero that you like, and ofcourse you can have multiple ones. Each class also has a multispec, since each hero has 4 skills, and for each skill you have 3 choices, SO, after prestige level 1 you can switch loadouts depending on match, for example the same hero could benefit from a different skillset depending on whether to go duel or do the battlefield arena. Up to you. I'm still levelling each class myself so I can see what each has to offer but I'm pretty sure there is a hero for any playstyle. Offence, Defence, Brute, assassins (dodge and hit) you name it.
Price, well that's open for discussion, You already pay for a AAA game, but if you want you can spend more money and buy outfits, all skills unlocked (you will get there by playing for free too!) But most importantly, you can buy a box with random gear, so there is that. If you spend money you can get much better game early in the game then if you go free to play. However, you would be an idiot if you spend that money on a hero that isn't prestige lvl1-3, so there is still a huge amount of ftp here. You can also buy champion status, like you would buy membership in a MMO for a limited time. This will grant you more XP, and grant your entire team a small xp buff. Is it worth it? I guess so, levelling goes a litlle faster, but not much. All in all, paying in this game will give you a lot of cosmetic stuff, but this is by no means a PtW game. You don't need to pay a dime after you bought the game, you will get it for free just by playing too.
So, here are my own personal pros/cons:
-Cons
1) Story is short
2) If you want to skip the grinding for gear, you must buy the boxes, which costs real money. Kinda rude for a game you bought in the first place.
3) Focus on multiplayer, and an even greater focus on PvP.
4) Progress is relatively slow. You need to be lvl 21 (first prestige) before the serious rewards enter the game. And there are only a few modes in the game atm, which makes it kinda restricted in options. (I'm not saying the modes suck!)
5) Connectivity. This is a real con. Often you will get no connection, or often you will lose connection before you get the rewards. That's really frustrating. So the online mode really needs to looked into. it is peer to peer atm, and although ubisoft promised dedicated servers, it's still PTP at this time. So expect a lot of disconnects, but for my regio I must admit the synchronisation works flawlessly. I have never been kicked out of a game.
6) PvP is awfull. It takes up more then half of this game as that is where the most players are, and it's nothing short of frustrating. If you want to like this, you'll need to exploit all the mechanics, and be pitched against weaker players. Which is no problem, since the only people playing PvP are those that have mastered the art of throwing you against stuff and abuse unblockables of their class. This game could be so great in PvP if it was just balanced, but instead it is the most frustrating and aggrevating pvp mode I have ever played. Because of this, this game will ultimately annoy the crap out of you, unless you want to spend time and become one of those guys. For me, it completely ruined the For honor experience.
7) Easy to learn, hard to master. After a few prestiges, even the bots get a level up and you can expect to die and lose everywhere. After a while the only way to play anymore is to abuse the mechanics which basically comes down to throw, throw, unblockable, throw, throw, and above all do not attack.
8) End game is pure frustration.
+Pro's
1) Graphics are stunning, seriously.
2) Controls take about 1-2h to get used to, which you may see as a con, but once you learnt how to block, a new world opens. This game is unique in this and it's absolutely fantastic. You constantly need to adapt your defence, but it's something you get used to very fast. Combine that with point 1 and you have very nice combat on screen. My kids for example love watching the fights. I love doing them.
3) co-op with swords. come on what's not to like. Nothing so fulfilling as killing your enemy first, then run over and help another player out. I'm loving the 2 vs 2 and 4 vs4 modes. You can revive fallen comrades, or you focus on the enemy which sometimes ends with 3 vs 1 or you as the lone surviver vs 2-4 enemies. Save the day and kill them all, or go revive teammates? Your choice.
4) Prestiging, the game is created in such a way that the higher level you earn, the more choice in gear/visuals you have. so you want all your favorite heroes at as high a level as possible. It really motivates you to level up!
5) Classes. they all play differently and although I'm determined to learn them all, you can feel instantly when a class suits you, or not. The gameplay is very intuïtive and you know if a class suits you after 2-5 duels. The game is VERY intuitive and you just have to try everyone and see who is to your liking.
6) The entire game is unique in it's style. I don't do this often but I'm totally buying the season packet. it's a bit expencive but I think this game is the best "beat em up" out there and I LOVE the co-op. Men vs AI. It is a great game, imagine a FPS but with swords.
I can recommend it to everyone that love pvp and all it's frustrations. But for everyone else, once you reach that point where you are tired of playing vs bots (even in co-op), this game will become extremely frustrating.
8.5/10 For me. With a litlle more content, modes this would be 9.5/10.

We should head round the mountain, she said, to the lake on the other side. We made it a good ways up the mountain before we hit a dead end, and we realized we had to go back. We were low on water by then, but we could maybe make it to Acro lake and if we were fast, get away before he spotted us.
We started down the hill. We made it a few hundred meters when Leana took a wrong step and began limping. I stayed with her awhile, but neither of us could afford to wait. I told her to evolve to Maia without me. Don't worry about me, I can make it to the lake.
Leana, I made it to the lake. On my last fifth of health and limping myself, but I made it and survived to Maia. I'll find you.

*IF YOU DON'T FEEL LIKE DOING A LOT OF READING THE VERDICT IS CLEARLY OUTLINED BELOW*
*NOTICE: I HAVE PLAYED THIS GAME MORE THAN STEAM HAS RECORDED*
A classic shooter that not only acted as a fore runner for FPS games to come, but is still a lot of fun to play. Visually, the game isn't super high def PS4/XBox One graphics (obviously), but the cartoony art style coupled with great design on the appearance of the monsters makes this a game that I find pleasing to look at, especially compared to other games which haven't aged well visually. The game runs well for the most part, though I do experience very brief, occasional slow downs, usually when there are a lot of monsters on screen. This brings me to the gameplay: "Doom" is still a very fun game to play (at least in my opinion). Its lack of aiming up and down or need to jump from spot to spot lets the player focus on high speed (I mean seriously fast) strafing and maneuvering to survive the demons that have sought to wreak havoc on our hero. And of course who can forget the lovely sound of heavy metal and shotguns?
Verdict
Doom is a fast paced FPS that pioneered the genre and is still great fun to this day. It's cartoony graphics have helped the game age suprisingly well visually, while its simple gameplay keeps the action fast and frenetic. Whether you want to play for a few minutes or a few hours, "Doom" will keep you entertained.

'The Isle' is an early access open world survival Game.
Until now you can choose from a variety of dinosaurs (22 at the moment, among them are the well known ones like Tyrannosaurus Rex, Carnotaurus, Stegosaurus and Triceratops ). Different Fractions besides them are planed.
In the game are right now two different game mechanics to choose from: Sandbox and Progression. Sandbox is
the easier mode. You can choose freely from all ,to the public released, creatures and play as them. You don't have to work yourself up and if you die you can easily choose them again. Progression is a mode where you have to 'grow' with your Dinosaur. For Example: You start as a Carnivore Dryo (later being replaced with Compy) and collect a certain amount of points until you can progress to the next tier, which would be eitherway the Austroraptor or the Herrerasaurus. Then you beginn to collect points for the next tier and so on. Until now you only gain points by surviving.
Before I give my personal opinion about the game, I suggest no matter what kind of reviews you read, don't let yourself influence from any of them. Instead you can, if you have certain doubts in matter of buying the game because of its looks, watch recent YouTube Videos of the game. The second thing you can do is following the development by joining The Isles Discord or watching Dev Streams on Twitch. I did it the same way, I found out about The Isle in december and purchased it in the first week of January, since then I'm following the game closely. The Developers are giving a great amount of insight into the current development, such as Map and Skin-Making, Programming and Modelling.
I personally adore The Isle in several aspects: Great Graphics. A beautiful environment.
Amazing and detailed Models with a great variety of beautiful skins.  A partially transparent Development.
Yes, there are a few bugs, but we got different ways to report them (such as report them in the bugtracker, make a thread in the steam forums or join the discord and report them in the appropiate chanel) , so that it can be taken care of as fast as possible.
In general: If you look at the whole picture, then you can see that until now 'The Isle' already came a long way and a lot has yet to come.

Pyre is a beautifully drawn and animated in the same art style of many of other Supergiant games, such as Bastion.  The design of the characters, the wagon your character comes to call home, and all of the lush environments mesh together well and will keep you involved in the world of Pyre.

There are many interesting characters that you meet on your journey of whom each have their own backgrounds and motivations that add greatly to the emotional depth that will push you to try your hardest during each 'game' to ensure the best outcome.  There are also many desicions made during the game that can affect your story, such as whether someone should stay with your group or if a dog should shave his mustache.
The gameplay of the 3 vs 3 games you have to compete in is fast and fun with each character having their own unique abilities that you can mix up to tailor to your style of gameplay.  This part of the game is so much fun I could play it for hours by itself without the storyline and still feel like I got my money's worth.
The only Con that I have with this game is I wish they would not introduce new members of your team right before a 'game' so you can have more time to see their worth.
Pyre as a package is a must buy.

That said - if you pick up the game and the "Rites" gameplay doesn't truly speak to you - it's best to ask for a refund at that point.  While I haven't finished the game I have played enough of it to reach various story "hooks" and I can say it's a sub-par narrative they gets fed to you exclusively through text.   There is a reason why I don't have visual novels in my gaming library and that's because if I wanted to read a novel - there are thousands of books out there that are much better than whatever Pyre is offering.
Total Biscuit once described Hand of Fate as greater than the sum of its parts, and I agree with that.  Pyre is sort of the inverse - its individual parts apart from the writing are all fantastic components within a vacuum but cumulatively they drag the rest down because they serve as a reminder of wasted effort.   The main "game" gameplay loop, if you look at it objectively is painfully shallow.  Until now Supergiant Games have made "indi" games that trip over the line into AAA quality.  Pyre's gameplay stumbles backward into the realm of mediocrity (polished mediocrity mind you) when you strip away all the visual spleandor.
The Audio is fantastic but it's heavily truncated compared to SG's previous iterations and just screams cut-corners.  The soundtrack is servicable but it does not meet Bastion's or Transistor's achiecements let alone exceed them.  The in-game SFX are very polished but there isn't much there that needs to be pushed.  It's a constant 3 vs 3 affair with generally the same 5 or so moves.
The game might be worth it if you just want to take a tour through some phenomenal art direction, but unless you are into very simplified "sports" prototypes (3 on 3, simple rules, simple mechanics, exploitable AI).  This is a Supergiant art demo with a boring gameplay loop tacked onto it and a ton of uninspired and uninteresting text tacked onto it.
Beyond the visuals and presentation - the only other good thing I can say about Pyre is that at least Supergiant Games got to make what I think will be viewed as a "dud" once the hype wears off to get it out of their system.  I hope they re-double their efforts for their next project because they are a fantastically talented developer.
Pyre, in my opinon, was a waste of that effort.  Also - watch your 2 hour play limit if you want to hold a refund.  The "inbetween" time between matches drags way more than it should and all the mechanics of the game aren't even revealed even at the 8 hour mark.
I wish the game was something more or something else.

Despite the amazing art style, and well thought out weapons systems/fighting, I can't really recommend the game because it's kind of boring and the plot is trite--in fact I quit about 3/4 of the way through. So let's start with what it does well. Most obviously, the art style exactly replicates the designs from old greek vases and urns. Everything from background, to the player, to enemies are rendered in this style, and when the player's health is slow, the screen gets more "distressed", like cracking pottery. So a real A+ on the art style.
Another thing that's really good is the weapons. There are many weapons divided into a number of different categories such as melee, ranged, and explosive. Some items can be crafted, others must be picked up. Weapons break, but generally only one of each weapon can be carried. This tends to encourage playing different weapons. The weapons have unique uses and some are better for some enemies than others.
The controls are good but not great. Standard actions are available, like rolling, jumping, etc. The weapons can be pointed in any direction based on the mouse. Everything feels a little awkward, but not terrible, and when I got used to the controls it was pretty easy.
Meanwhile, the standard enemies and obstacles are pretty easy to deal with. There are a few minor puzzles which are simple enough. The bosses are physically quite large and can be challenging: like old school games, each requires a different strategy.
Given all the things this game does well, why don't I like it? Well, simply put, the story is terrible. This is not always a problem in games--many games don't need plot because the whole point is the action. Well, this game is basically some combo of metroidvania and RPG. Everything from the art style to the careful progression really feels epic--and epic needs a good story. But all they could come up with was the standard "human tries to defeat the Gods one by one", and that got pretty boring pretty quickly. They have small side-quests that would have been perfect to flesh out the story, but no, nothing really. And some exposition is lazily added through these stones commerating the gods.
As a counter example: the Banner Saga was also artistically interesting and epic in progression, but with less polished combat and mechanics than this game. But that game had a really amazing story and took every opportunity to really hook the player in. These guys really missed a good opportunity--especially since they did so many things right.
I am definitely up for playing a sequel if they can address the story issue.

Story: The story is quite interesting, it attracts me most of the time, wanting to know what would happen, and yet again, decision making somewhat affects the storyline too. Why I gave a rating of 9 instead of 10: After the story ended (for the first time), I was actually hoping for the gameplay to continue, so I could start over, but with better setup, while increasing the difficulty of the game, most importantly is to change my decisions throughout the second gameplay, and see how the story goes in a different way. I'm surprised I hadn't heard of this game until seeing it in a discovery queue full of obscure stuff. This was a real gem. Bought it on sale because it looked nice, but some negative reviews almost kept me away. Really glad I decided to check it out. It's a solid platformer with very few things you could really call flaws. It's not ridiculously difficult, but there are a lot of challenging moments and added challenges from achievements. The controls felt a bit stiff at first, but they're fairly standard for this sort of game, and I got used to them easily enough. Graphics, music, writing, all great. Animations in particular were fantastic.
There are only two things that bothered me. One being that for all the buttons I had on my controller, I only used like... four? You end up with a lot of things you can do, but not a lot of buttons for inputs. In particular, I found dashing to be a problem sometimes, because you have to push attack and jump at the same time, and sometimes you'll just end up attacking or jumping, or when you try to jump and attack quickly, sometimes you'll dash. The second thing is that the boss rush has some very weird bugs going on. It seems like your first attempt at it works fine, but if you try again without completely closing out the game and opening it again, you'll die after getting your final time, and it won't save it. What's even weirder is that one time I was somehow sent to the Japanese version of the game, but it only showed one of the frames from the level select pictures. I eventually figured out that pushing right enough times would bring me back to the English version, but for a second I thought my save was broken, because even restarting didn't fix it. These were the only bugs I encountered though, and I figured them out, so they didn't hurt my experience much, but a fix to that would be nice.
Anyway, I highly recommend this game. Especially right now on sale. If it looks at all appealing to you from the videos, you'll probably love it. It was exactly what I was hoping for.

It has been many years since I had my phase of Bejeweled 3 addiction, and those are fond memories indeed.
I'll review Bejeweled 3 here as I remember it.
Bejeweled 3 is the amazing sequel and massive improvement to Bejeweled 2 that none of us would have seen coming. Bringing with it surprising, positive innovations while still preserving the option of the great core gameplay of Bejeweled that we have always known and loved. There's not really much to be said about the gameplay other than it's Bejeweled, but better and expanded, taken in brilliant new directions while preserving the old.
The presentation of it all brings the experience as a whole to such a greater level than we'd have ever imagined. The new visual splendor is exciting, pumping, and filled with eye-candy while at the same time being beautiful and serene, and most importantly, still conveys the gameplay without obstruction or serious distraction.
It is accompanied by magnificent audio design, with the sound effects adding that satisfying edge to each and every move, while being clear and distinctive to give more feedback as to the state of the game and our actions within. with more skilled matches giving more and more satisfying and exciting audio responses. The soundtrack is simply phenomenal, a beautiful collection of tracks by demoscene composer Peter Hajba that both serve to immerse you in the experience of the game while also conveying the mood, ranging from blissful in the Zen soundtracks to heart-racing in the Ice and Lightning modes.
Bejeweled 3 is an incredible example of taking a simple, previously lighthearted and arcadey 2D puzzle game with no story, no defined world, no characters, and all that and turning it in to a wholly immersive experience, bringing with it a sense of awe and so many different feelings of either bliss, rage, rage, or hecticness all based around the core swapping-gems gameplay.
The only shortcomings that come to mind are generally in regards to aging. The visuals can feel a bit low res now on a big screen or high res display. But that's reallly the only possible criticism here.
It was the real Popcap's last game before their tragic acquisition and subsequent adulteration. And what a magnificent note to go out on it was!
Rest in peace Popcap Games: 2000 - 2011.
Verdict: BUY IT - even at its non-sale price, it will provide massive amounts of value and fun. It makes an excellent addition to every Steam library.

Update 1-10-2017. Been doing quite some PvP lately since pve was basically mastered. And it completely ruined the game for me. Expect hours and hours of frustration. I was looking out for this game thanks to the trailers. Truth be told, I was expecting a different game. A single player game I guess.
I was pleasantly welcomed by doing the story, which is great. It's challenging and it looks awesome. Other then that I also loved the story on its own
However I soon discovered that once you finish the story, all that's left is multiplayer. And the Story is on the short side, so I was dissapointed as PvP isn't my thing.
Then I gave it a shot and boy, do I love this game. I rarely do Pvp, but that's ok as you can do EVERYTHING as co op instead. And that's something I absolutely love. 1v1, 2v2, 4v4, point capture. All humans vs the AI. YES!
So with playability after story covered, it was time to look into the different heroes. And different they are! You have 3 "races" and each has 4 classes. Each one is unique. So that means you have plenty of choice (12) to find a hero that you like, and ofcourse you can have multiple ones. Each class also has a multispec, since each hero has 4 skills, and for each skill you have 3 choices, SO, after prestige level 1 you can switch loadouts depending on match, for example the same hero could benefit from a different skillset depending on whether to go duel or do the battlefield arena. Up to you. I'm still levelling each class myself so I can see what each has to offer but I'm pretty sure there is a hero for any playstyle. Offence, Defence, Brute, assassins (dodge and hit) you name it.
Price, well that's open for discussion, You already pay for a AAA game, but if you want you can spend more money and buy outfits, all skills unlocked (you will get there by playing for free too!) But most importantly, you can buy a box with random gear, so there is that. If you spend money you can get much better game early in the game then if you go free to play. However, you would be an idiot if you spend that money on a hero that isn't prestige lvl1-3, so there is still a huge amount of ftp here. You can also buy champion status, like you would buy membership in a MMO for a limited time. This will grant you more XP, and grant your entire team a small xp buff. Is it worth it? I guess so, levelling goes a litlle faster, but not much. All in all, paying in this game will give you a lot of cosmetic stuff, but this is by no means a PtW game. You don't need to pay a dime after you bought the game, you will get it for free just by playing too.
So, here are my own personal pros/cons:
-Cons
1) Story is short
2) If you want to skip the grinding for gear, you must buy the boxes, which costs real money. Kinda rude for a game you bought in the first place.
3) Focus on multiplayer, and an even greater focus on PvP.
4) Progress is relatively slow. You need to be lvl 21 (first prestige) before the serious rewards enter the game. And there are only a few modes in the game atm, which makes it kinda restricted in options. (I'm not saying the modes suck!)
5) Connectivity. This is a real con. Often you will get no connection, or often you will lose connection before you get the rewards. That's really frustrating. So the online mode really needs to looked into. it is peer to peer atm, and although ubisoft promised dedicated servers, it's still PTP at this time. So expect a lot of disconnects, but for my regio I must admit the synchronisation works flawlessly. I have never been kicked out of a game.
6) PvP is awfull. It takes up more then half of this game as that is where the most players are, and it's nothing short of frustrating. If you want to like this, you'll need to exploit all the mechanics, and be pitched against weaker players. Which is no problem, since the only people playing PvP are those that have mastered the art of throwing you against stuff and abuse unblockables of their class. This game could be so great in PvP if it was just balanced, but instead it is the most frustrating and aggrevating pvp mode I have ever played. Because of this, this game will ultimately annoy the crap out of you, unless you want to spend time and become one of those guys. For me, it completely ruined the For honor experience.
7) Easy to learn, hard to master. After a few prestiges, even the bots get a level up and you can expect to die and lose everywhere. After a while the only way to play anymore is to abuse the mechanics which basically comes down to throw, throw, unblockable, throw, throw, and above all do not attack.
8) End game is pure frustration.
+Pro's
1) Graphics are stunning, seriously.
2) Controls take about 1-2h to get used to, which you may see as a con, but once you learnt how to block, a new world opens. This game is unique in this and it's absolutely fantastic. You constantly need to adapt your defence, but it's something you get used to very fast. Combine that with point 1 and you have very nice combat on screen. My kids for example love watching the fights. I love doing them.
3) co-op with swords. come on what's not to like. Nothing so fulfilling as killing your enemy first, then run over and help another player out. I'm loving the 2 vs 2 and 4 vs4 modes. You can revive fallen comrades, or you focus on the enemy which sometimes ends with 3 vs 1 or you as the lone surviver vs 2-4 enemies. Save the day and kill them all, or go revive teammates? Your choice.
4) Prestiging, the game is created in such a way that the higher level you earn, the more choice in gear/visuals you have. so you want all your favorite heroes at as high a level as possible. It really motivates you to level up!
5) Classes. they all play differently and although I'm determined to learn them all, you can feel instantly when a class suits you, or not. The gameplay is very intuïtive and you know if a class suits you after 2-5 duels. The game is VERY intuitive and you just have to try everyone and see who is to your liking.
6) The entire game is unique in it's style. I don't do this often but I'm totally buying the season packet. it's a bit expencive but I think this game is the best "beat em up" out there and I LOVE the co-op. Men vs AI. It is a great game, imagine a FPS but with swords.
I can recommend it to everyone that love pvp and all it's frustrations. But for everyone else, once you reach that point where you are tired of playing vs bots (even in co-op), this game will become extremely frustrating.
8.5/10 For me. With a litlle more content, modes this would be 9.5/10.

So before I get into the meat of it, I think Friday the 13th is a 4.5 out of 10 game. "But Mongoose, why? It's SO GOOD." Friday the 13th could've been "so good", but it falls flat for me due to game breaking bugs, balance issues, and generally lackluster gameplay. I've been looking forward to this game for almost a year now, and to see how it is, coming out unfinished, I'm disappointed. In 3/5 of your games, you will have the car flip over while you're trying to escape, you'll be caught in a visual glitch and unable to move, you'll just have a really bad time for most of the games you get in. Jason can glitch through the map, and end up dying, and completely ruin the experience! When playing the counselor, you can get 1-shot by Jason if he grabs you, unless you're one of the lucky few who can instantly get 3 pocket knives, and know where they are regardless of if you spawn near them or not. And playing Jason, people can just loop through houses with windows that can't be broken, and they just keep running around, as if they have infinite stamina. That brings up another point, stamina. I get that people who play the slow Jasons praise this feature, I'm I'm one of them, but most people don't play the slow Jasons, they play the jogger Jasons, and catch up to you in a flash. Unless you find a house with an unbreakable window, you'll run out, he'll get you, and you'll die, and no one will help you because most of the time, no one will understand you! A lot of games I get in have these Japanese, Russian, Korean, foreign dudes that don't speak a lick of English! And part of this game requires good communication! I get that as an indie developer, you can't get servers put in seperate countries, but you could've done something, anything, if you'd have taken longer to release. It feels unfinished, Jimmy, and I feel like I'm playing an early access game with a $40 price tag! This game is a $20 game at BEST! Not even Dead By Daylight is this busted! Sure, it has lots of DLC, but at least there's a gesture button to help with those foreign dudes! At least if the generators pop, there's no chance for them to suddenly not open the gates, barring your exit! With friends, the bugs are funny, you can laugh at them, but not when there's random people who you have no comfort in joking with, it's just annoying. With friends, the game goes up to a 5 out of 10, but it's still low because of the bugs and $40 price tag. If I didn't want to give the game more of a chance, then I would've refunded it, but I wanted to play it on the off chance my friends take interest, so I can't refund it, and right now, it feels like a waste of 40 bucks. Overall disappointment. Wait until the game's actually finished before buying it.

I've been playing this game since it first came out. I really enjoyed it when I played it at the very beginning. I think it has potential, obviously it is in early access right now and needs a massive amount of work.
Things that need to be fixed:
-Plant/Water placement.
Plant/water locations are too far away for starter herbivore characters, which have high hunger/water requirements. It is likely that you will spawn in a poor locaion and die simply because the spawn point is too far from any food. (distance is too great or blocked off by steep mountains which are impassable if you are playing as the starter herbivore)
-Navigation system
This game desperately needs an in-game navigation system. Using the debug panel to navigate the map is not a great user experience. Try adding a nav window to the HUD.
-UI
The recent UI overhaul is nice in terms of making the menus a bit more navigable. However I think artistically, the UI could use another pass. Some of the buttons/2D menu assets look very sloppy and poorly drawn. The current group invite system/management leaves the player unclear who is in their group if they lose sight of them. Chat window navigation could be made clearer as well.
-Prioritiies
Instead of adding new dinosaurs every few months, try fixing issues that affect the core gameplay. That means fixing bugs/improving the UI/UX, and balancing the core game.
-The Community
Some servers seem to be controlled by a core group of players that grind the game all day. They get the most powerful dinosaurs and kill everything they see on sight. This makes the game hard to access for casual players. So you end up spawning 10 times within the same play session only to have the same people kill you every time, unprovoked. Not sure what to do about this, or if it is solvable.

Pyre was not at all what I was expecting. It’s a “party-based role-playing game” just as they say, but the actual gameplay looks closer to a soccer/basketball hybrid than most conventional fantasy games do. And… that’s actually really okay.
Each “Rite” as Pyre calls them has teams of 3 facing off against eachother to douse the opponent’s flame. Each flame has an amount of health, and scoring points will remove health from it until a Pyre is extinguished.
Different races serve as different classes – each class has two skill trees, and these skills can change up gameplay immensely. Also, each class has stats that make them inherently faster, have larger auras, etc.
Pyre has fast and crazy gameplay that is fun to play against the CPU, or a friend – unfortunately, there is only local multiplayer. No online multiplayer is a major bummer, as it would be fun to challenge friends online.
Pyre also has a full-fledged single player campaign that sees your team of exiles trying to gain their freedom by performing rites. The story is well written, and the art and music are amazing. There is too much downtime in what feels like padding between the “Rites” and the announcer can get a little annoying at times. Lots of decisions change the outcome, and the developers intended you to live with your mistakes- though save scumming is possible.
Definitely recommend this for someone who wants to play a unique fantasy-themed ballgame with RPG elements, or for someone who can suffer such mechanics for a beautiful and heartfelt campaign through the beautifully drawn but dangerous purgatory known as the Downside.

Nether is one of my favorite fps out there. I started again after the steam sale, and was a little bummed see that they had wiped the Global inventory a second time.
However after picking up a pipe sniper another played had left on the ground in the safezone I had the weapon I needed.
This game takes a lot of strategy in terms of picking a prime location to set up an ambush on other suspecting players. I picked the roof of a building near the central part of the map which I figured would have a decent amount of foot traffic as players traveled between safezones.
Boy was a right 15 min after scouting nearby terrain I spotted a threeman team chilling in the middle of a nearby street. I took my one shot in the chamber and took out the guy who looked most geared and watched as a bounty rewarded message popped on the screem and an explosion of loot rained from his body. Instead of his two buddies picking up guns their companion dropped, they tried rushing me with melee weapons. I took them out easily with the sniper.
I ended up picking up the loot from all three and ended up getting 3 reaper blades and mag dr-15. Using the cru's I got from the blades I have been able to completely fill out my Gi with snipers and assault rifles taken from the mindless players that pay too much attention on the ground level instead of watching the roof tops.
Once you build up a decent supply of guns this game becomes more similar to far cry 3 open world style fps with multiplayer thrown in in terms of picking where you want to try to set up an ambush.
You never know when /where you will run into other players so you really have to watch your corners as you explore or you will die very easily.
Most of the reviews I've seen are negative due to the fact that people die and lose their stuff to bandits like myself, and to that I say in order to progres through nether, in terms of building an arsenal, you have to play smart. You can easily recognize the ways that players traverse the map based on the locations of safezones.
When you hear a gunshot you can usually predict where a player will go based on the direction of the shot in relation to the nearest safezone.
If you really enjoy open world pvp this is the game for you. Just have patience you'll get your arsenal built up after playing smart and taking out a few n00bish players.

I'll start with my overall rating 8/10.
Soma made some great improvements on previous releases by Frictional Games but could still use some work.
10/10 Monsters/Atmosphere/Sounds/Music/Effects
The biggest improvement is to the quality of the monsters. SOMA, in my opinion, has the scariest monsters of any release by Frictional Games to date and a huge improvement from Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs. The incredible 10/10 monster graphics, sounds, AI, atmosphere, and screen distortions will leave even the bravest players feeling threatened. I think this is an especially important improvement as many horror fans are getting more and more used to scary games and need extra scary encounters to feel the same effect that hooked them to begin with.
9/10 Story
The story was another excellent feature as it usually is in releases by Frictional Games. Although it takes a while to piece together, the story is a very clever, creative, and believable one in which you wake up in a foreign world that causes you to question who you are and what it means is human.
5/10 Puzzles/Maps
My biggest disappointment with SOMA was the large disorenting maps and confusing puzzles throughout the game. I all too often found myself running around trying to figure out where I needed to go or what puzzle I needed to solve, and for me this was very discomforting. One might argue that this provides a more realistic experience, however, it left me feeling without a sense of achievement. Instead of feeling like I conquered my way past the monsters and obstacles, I felt like I blindly managed to get through. And this was disappointing. I think Frictional Games could look back to one of thier best successes, Amnesia: The Dark Descent, and remember what made it so great. The complexity of the puzzles combined with the invetory system and occasional supporting note left players feeling like they had both understood and overcame an obstacle. In SOMA, I experienced that a trial and error approach is often taken where players are guided to tinker with machines that are highlighted with the interaction icon but may not really know why. Additionally, in navigating the large maps I often felt highly pressured to follow pathways and lights instead of exploring, mostly because I had no clues as to where I was going and was discouraged to explore by the vastness of the area and poor lighting. I beleive the great feeling you get from playing Amnesia: The Dark Descent comes from familiarizing yourself with the environment and finding items by exploring every corner of the castle and logically solving most obstacles that block your path all the while avoiding horrific monsters. SOMA to me felt more like running around, sometimes guided, and trying random things while avoiding horrific monsters, although there were a few exceptions where you did have to explore and gather items or complete some task.

Rainbow Six Siege is a Objective-Based Multiplayer FPS where you fight in competetive matches 5 vs 5 either as an attacker or as an defender.
My Review is solely on the game at this state, but most things i say will probably never change or are implemented in the whole core gameplay.
First of all the starting process is already a pain because i have a steam account and have to use another account in another platform from ubisoft. This is a hassle because the uplay launcher is so terribly unstable and the servers arent that good either. Steam friends dont carry over and you have to readd them .
The gameplay is pretty good tough, it is really fun to play as different classes and they counter other classes or are building upon each other in your team.Some classes are balancing wise better than others tough. Most of the walls and ceilings are destroyable to a high extenct that even bullet holes are left over so you can make your own peeking positions. The objectives are pretty basic, king of the hill, defuse the bomb or save hostage. Fun but nothing really new.
The game is set in two faces defending and attacking, each time as attacker you send in drones to search for the enemy spawn place because it resets every round and can be on a totally different spot on the map. But that face can get kinda boring after a couple times you have seen it.

Vicariously view violent Violette vehemently victimize valueless Nazis. I’m not sure why I went with the unneeded alliteration but I’m not sure why the developers went with velvet. Maybe they were trying to turn Violet into velvet for some reason but…whatever…
Velvet Assassin takes places in the early/mid 1940s. You’re a British assassin named Violette Summer who’s based off, in first name, hairstyle, and background only, of real world British assassin
. Violette single handedly either takes out several high ranking Nazi leaders (who didn’t exist) or helped lead to the destruction of several Nazi outposts including the real-life mission
. She does this with her well placed knife and a Nazi jugular vein. She also uses a silenced pistol but …ugh. More on this unfortunate mechanic later.
Stealth is both very good and very bad at the same time. Apparently, Nazi’s were very blind individuals. A light shade in otherwise broad daylight can keep them from noticing you. It seems odd that any darkness can be that good in a, mostly, realistic stealth game. The game does have a higher difficulty so if you want to skip the, “Does Violette have special shadow moving powers?” go ahead play that. I hear it’s painfully real. The game also has ‘Morphine Mode’, which allows you to travel unnoticed or get a face to face kill cam. It might seem like a supernatural power but you learn the first 10 missions are all flashbacks so morphine mode is a foggy memory of how Violette got that kill. The final two are “current time” missions.
As you go through missions you find collectibles and hidden achievements (found through exploration) which, when you reach 1000 exp, allows you to upgrade a stat, either morphine mode; which increases syringe count and length, stealth; which allows you move faster, or strength; which makes you tankier. The collectibles are various war medals and paraphernalia, some of which have interesting back stores but I feel like there could have been expanded to allow for more backstory. You might start feeling sympathy for Nazis through. There’re a few instances where the horrors of war appear all too human and you feel a little guilty as poor Gretchen won’t be seeing her husband because of you. They may be literal Nazi’s but they still dream and love like the good ol’ boys in [insert your country flag colors here]. That’s one of the things the game does really well. The carnage of WWII is evident in every aspect of the game. Dead bodies litter the streets of Warsaw, Poland. Several children are apart of the body count as they hang in various trees in France. Some enemies are even given a soul when they wish none of this has happened and just want to go back home; not everyone follows the leader in war. There’s even one letter where the writer says he’s ready to die due to the nightmare reality.
VA has 12 missions which average out an hour of play time (not sure if time resets on death). Checkpoints are all over the place but getting to them can be very painful. The slowness of the game is apparent when you have to kill a significant amount of enemies in a less than straight forward way where you get caught, die and have to try again. Missions like level 6 might be a game killer if you’re not dedicated. The first 10 levels are wonderful, albeit a crawl at times. “Realistic” stealth mechanics where hiding in the shadows, behind a crate, or disguised as the only female SS officer in the game are the way to victory as there’s not enough ammo to go Rambo. That all changes in the last two levels and therein is where the game devolves into suffering.
You see, Velvet Assassin stops being about stealth and turns into a third person shooter. This would be fine but the shooting aspects are very poor. The crosshair is there but bullets don’t always go where you’d think, enemies can be randomly resistant to damage, and general aim abilities are just awful. You know how many games have ice levels and you don’t stop when you want to stop? That’s what aiming in this game feels like. If you move a little, it doesn’t move but if you move a lot you just turned 360 degrees while barely trying. This can be mitigated by using a mouse but even then it needs a lot of work. To exacerbate the terrible aiming, the stealth mechanic goes away. Enemies are suddenly more likely to see you, even in deep shadows and getting enemies alone where you can get a knife kill is nearly impossible and it comes from nowhere. You can get through all but one or two levels in the first 10 without shooting anyone but suddenly it’s the only way to progress.
Along with the sudden genre shift, the developers tried to add some sex to the game. Violette stops wearing jackets and black leather ‘armor’ and now dons only a white negligée (and the velvet in Velvet Assassin) due to story reasons. She’s also very shiny for, uh, ‘plot’. It turns a hardnosed female assassin into a male fetish. There’s no option to get dressed and even in the credit epilogue, she’s in her underwear. It’s like the last two levels were done by a different team. The game could have been great but due to the ending levels, it turns itself into mediocre at best.
As for non-gameplay aspects: Voice acting is nice. Our Heroine sounds smooth and pleasant and at no point do you ever wish for her to shut-up. Maybe it’s the English accent (from a New York born, German -for five years- raised woman) or the lower tones but I’d like to hear
more often. The German enemies spoke German (with subtitles if you don’t speak the language) so there’s some immersion for ya.
Music is…eh. You hear the sound of gunfire too often and in places where you shouldn’t be hearing gunfire. It can also throw you off and make you think someone saw you and it's combat time. Otherwise, it’s all atmospheric. It ramps up when you’ve been spotted and it always makes me feel like I screwed up when I hear it. Not sure if that was the purpose but that’s the outcome so, to be honest, I’m digging it. There are no official sources so here’re some
videos. There are actually more tracks than I thought and there’s less than one page in the link.
The art helps contribute perfectly to the doom and gloom of war. There are no vibrant colors and blue skies are replaced by a dark, dirty, orange. There aren’t even any stars in the sky at night. Everything else is stone, iron, and ground. No hope, no freedom, no future. Welcome to war. That being said, the Paris skyline from the river Seine (or what I think is the river) circa 1943 looks beautiful even in high overcast and fog.
The game has its sufferable flaws but for .49 USD cents which is what I paid for it during a summer sale (so the price of 8-16 cards), it’s well worth it. It’s a slow plough through the first 10 levels (which is what to expect from a stealth game) and the third person shooting genre change makes the game way less fun so at full price, don’t buy it; it’s not worth it. I really wish I could recommend at full price but my frustrations at needing to relearn the game 5/6ths of the way in makes It hard. File it under cult classic.

I suspect that the reason this game isn't talked about more is because just looking at screenshots it doesn't stick out as particularly special. But this game should be talked about more, because besides one really frustrating level, this game is near perfect in its execution of solid Metroidvania combat and exploration.
The Rabbit-Man Jonathon comes out of the box feeling powerful, with an array of long-range attacks that nullify projectiles and combo into aerials for which you are rewarded with health and mana. While the basic enemies tend to just be obstacles as you plow through the game's hallways, bosses have recognizable but tricky patterns to put your tools to use. As you get upgraded through the game's collectables, every sub-weapon adds welcome tools that cover the weaknesses the basic moveset has, and minor differences in scale - such as increases in attack damage - can be obtained from your treasure hunting. Eventually as you explore previously completed levels, your new movement abilities and gear make you feel godlike. It's a fantastic power fantasy tempered by progressively increasing challenge to keep you feeling accomplished.
Driving this gameplay is a cute story following the archetypal treasure hunt, made more fun by lovable characters and a tongue-in-cheek sense of humor. The banter between Jonathan and his support character Jack and his rival Andre was highly entertaining for me. With that said, the radio conversations constantly pop up within the gameplay, so if the writing fails to appeal to you I could see this as being a detractor. The dialog is skippable through a fast-forward style button press, though there will still be a pause while it's being skipped. To me though, the character interactions are one of the highlights of the game. It contextualizes the gameplay and makes the good moments great.
The level structure is mission-based, so it's closer to something like Mega Man Zero or Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia rather than Symphony of the Night. While a lot of the game's unlockables require you to return to levels already completed, it captures the spirit of exploration rather than strictly being a matter of backtracking. This is helped by nothing obtained by revisits being completely required for the game's completion (though, especially on the game's hard mode it certainly helps to get them.) And, as I mentioned, I thought it was fun to revisit and tackle old challenges with the power obtained from later in the game.
The one major complaint I have about Pharaoh Rebirth is in regards to a specific mission that tries to change things up with an on-rails car section. It's bad, and it's required to progress. There isn't enough screen space to really telegraph when you need to jump, so the game uses a sound cue instead. However even knowing that a jump is coming, the timing of when to jump is something that I only mastered through strict trial and error. Since death throws you to continue screen and drops you back in the previous checkpoint this means a lot of replaying sections until either you figure out the rhythm of the sound cue or accomplish the task through rote memorization. In a short burst the vehicle section might not have been terrible, but culminating on its issues, it's long enough to be exhausting. I felt like the missions that followed were totally worth slogging through it, but a slog it was.
But in spite of that one blight, I think Pharaoh Rebirth + is otherwise an ideal accomplishment of its genre. It certainly deserves attention, and comes highly recommended from me.

I’m Jackie Estacado and I am the host for the Darkness. It’s a rough life fighting it from taking me over completely but man does it have some sweet powers. There has been some bad consequences though like losing the love of my life Jenny. I’m dealing with that and now some brotherhood wants to take the Darkness from me. Not going to happen on my watch.
In the Darkness II you are still suffering from the loss of Jenny from the first game. You have held the Darkness at bay for a while but now some group called the Brotherhood wants to take it from you using a device called the siphon which will suck the Darkness out of you. Well you aren’t going to let this happen because it’s just bad news for everyone.
There are a variety of ways to play through the levels fighting the Brotherhood. You can quad-wield now unlike the first game which gives you options like rip a car door off and use it as a shield while still being able to carry two guns and whip people with you other Darkness tentacle. Special executions can be done by grabbing an enemy with the tentacles, while he is stunned, and rip them apart for more health or ammo. You can also upgrade your powers via a skill tree wheel to add more possibilities like an execution that makes a shield from the enemy or had a Darkness swarm which stuns enemies for a short time.
Unlike the first game you only have one Darkling to help you but he has more of a personality than before. He adds a little humor to everything which lightens the dark mood a bit. Guns are your standard fair ranging from pistols, smgs, assault rifles, and shotguns. You can upgrade you guns to buy adding bigger clips, faster reloads, and shooting Darkness essence through them.
The game does look good most of the time with its comic book pastel art style. Environments seemed to be pretty bland though and felt like I was just going through a reskinned map each level. Enemies were also basic with pretty much the same five skins all the time.
Story wise I wasn’t too impressed and sometimes felt like I was just pushing forward to finish the game so it was no longer in my backlog. I just felt like it was just missing something the whole time. The endings, there are two choices, were both mediocre and not fulfilling. Expected a bigger finish than it was. You can replay it again in new game+ which lets you keep all your unlocked powers. I just didn’t feel the pull to do it though.
Darkness II also has a co-op campaign mode called Vendetta you can play with up to four players. It’s basically a side story to the campaign where you can control your choice of four different characters who have their own special Darkness powers. All these characters also have skills you can upgrade to make them more powerful. There is another mode you can pick through Vendetta called The Hit List which is basically shorter missions using the Vendetta campaign levels. Both these modes are cool to play with some friends but doesn’t really add much to the game.
Overall if you’re a fan of the comic and enjoyed the first Darkness then you’ll want to check this one out. It could have been much more without the co-op stuff and just focused on the single player portion of the game but it is still a decent game to play.

This was a sweet, sweet experience and a more intricate/expansive one than I've expected honestly. While this VN might not be long by Japanese standards, it took me full two evening to complete it and I was pleasantly surprised with the story variation and the quality of content it offered.
I will maybe start by addressing a few obvious concerns. First, the game indeed features a childish crush between two very young girls, but never crosses the line into uncomfortable territories - everything that happens between them is really cute and innocent and the romantic ending offers an epilogue set a decade later, with some very, very mild "sexual content" (also known as a kissing CG). There's really no reason to freak out.
Second, while the aesthetic might be diabetes-inducing, it's a well-written and compelling little story (although obviously comedic and at times pretty absurd because of that), that should be satisfying for even more demanding, mature readers, if they're not allergic to cute things. It has a completely different tone that most of Ebi-Hime's work, but it's still very well done,
Third, it's pretty serious about it's main theme of sweets and food, but doesn't go overboard - it didn't bore me with long scenes of preparing meals and "foodgasms" like some anime series did in the past.
All this combines with fun characters and gorgeous art really made it a satisfying, relaxing experience for me. There are things that could be criticized - like Rie being a bit too mature and smart for a second-grader, some grammar mistakes and minor errors or the somewhat forgettable music. In the end though, it's one of the best short, casual VNs I've read to date and I can wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who doesn’t hate yuri or comedic slice-of-life stories.

It's a shame that this game has been missed by everyone.  I have played most every metroidvania on Steam, and a lot of others, and this is among the best.  It may not have as much of the RPG elements that I enjoy from the Castlevanias, but the action and exploration are excellent.  Many metroidvanias suffer a little bit from pacing and low platforming action, which is where this game shines. The game focuses on learning boss patterns and capitalizing on their vulnerable moments and works as well as classics like Mega Man.
Some have commented that this game is not a Metroidvania.  I would argue that it definitely is.  The format is similar to Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia or the paintings in Portrait of Ruin.   You choose maps or levels to enter, but they are large and follow the traditional metroidvania format.  You learn skills that give you access to more areas, and the game does a great job of providing incentive to return to past levels to encounter new challenges and find secrets.
The sub-weapons are the highlight of the game. There are many to be discovered and all of them are useful in particular situations.  I often found myself stopping as I started a boss fight or challenging room to re-evaluate my strategy with a new sub-weapon.
I didn't have high expectations for the story in a game with a rabbit as the main character.  However, I was happily suprised that the story is actually better than about any metroidvania I've played.  The characters are likeable and funny, although it doesn't feel forced.
Last of all, the music catchy and cool. i found myself humming the songs throughout the day after beating a dungeon.
Support an excellent indie game!  If you like action platformers or metroidvanias, you will not regret it.

I find it appropriate that you play as an archaeologist since this game scratches that treasure-hunting itch just right. Krobon has this talent for genuinely interesting level design that makes you want to explore every nook and cranny in the hopes of finding secret rooms and ancient artifacts.
I also think that the characters are adorable and the story pretty funny in a cutesy kind of way. Jonathan's move set makes sense to his character and every new ability you learn encourages you to revisit previous levels in the hopes of reaching that platform that was previously out of your grasp.
There's even a Jojo reference in it!
I did have a few gripes, though:
-There are a few items you can permanently miss due to not performing a certain action at a certain time, which could be a big pain if you're a completionist.
-Level 5 is probably the worst level in the game as it's a driving section that requires precise jumping to get through alive. As a result, I probably spent a good two hours or so in this area alone, intentionally crashing my jeep so I could restart and collect that last golden piece I barely noticed as I sped towards a cliff at seventy mph. I admire the designer wanting to change the gameplay up a bit and, to be fair, Level 5 is not agonizing or impossible to complete. But compared to the rest of the game, I didn't find it nearly as fun to play, despite the really cool boss at the end.
-I experienced some slowdown, though this might be a technical issue on my part and not the fault of the designer.
I do love this game overall, though, and plan on replaying it for a 100% run. If you like exploration-based platformers with good music and quirky characters, give this a whirl.

Game in the akward position of being good enough to deserve some recognition, but not amazing enough to actually get it. Kinda sad, if you think about it.
Pharaoh Rebirth is something I would call a quasi-metroidvania style game. It's design and gameplay loop is very much similar to the Shantae and the Pirate's Curse. Yes, it is a platformer with unlockable items that let you get into new places and you are allowed to do some backtracking, but game's world isn't seamless and it is divided into separate levels. It's scope is slightly smaller than those of Shantae's but the core game structure is safe, sound and works reasonably well.
There is a lot of things to like in the game, even if those aren't always on the highest level of the genre. Combat is very satisfying, with good selection of moves and subweapons at the disposal of sympathetic, bunny-like protagonist. Enemies, bosses and level design also present a great deal of care and they are generally aspects that don't make me point out any immediate nitpicks.
Artstyle is also a strong point of the title, with details and colors reminding me a lot of Cave Story. I would bet that for the Japanesee dev of Pharaoh, that well known, respected title was a source of inspiration. While sprites are amazing, I was a little disappointed by the level tiles and decorations that can get repetive and bland, making some levels boring to lot at. Similarly, music not always sold me on the game, but few tunes are really good and leave a good impression overall.
As for the major complains I have with the game, I would point out some problems with controls and the story. While combat is satisfying, I believe that jumps and movement of the main character could use some tuning up. Leaps are floaty and not very responsive, which is extremely jarring if you recently came back from 2D platformers with super-snappy controls like Sonic or Freedom Planet. As for the plot: it's not bad in reality, but sometimes there is a Megaman X5 syndrome creeping in, with constant dialog boxes that can hurt the flow of the levels.
Game is short, but I believe it deserves a little bit more love, even if it isn't in the same league as some other indie blockbusters. I really can appreciate a honest effort put here on the display, but I game isn't exactly selling hot and I can get an idea why it is. Nowadays "Being Good" isn't enough to gain attention unfortunately. Never less, if this game somehow made you read this review, you can consider buying this for a full price or for a slight sale. Value proposition for Pharaoh Rebirth is on the reasonable level and I assume that this dev would appreciate a helping hand.
PS This game has actual, high quality JoJo’s Bizzare Adventure reference in the form of a certain subweapon. You can never pass or not mention a good JoJo reference.

Incredibly cute VN that shifts the focus on romantic relationships between adults to the budding friendship between two children.
Strawberry Vinegar features a 9 year old girl named Rie who is responsible, cynical and deep down very lonely. She is one day visited by Licia - a demon from Hell. Licia demands that Rie make her delicious food throughout the course of a week or she will reap her soul. Licia is here on a "vacation" to see what earth is like, and Rie becomes her caregiver throughout the course of a six day period. Although resisitive to having Licia around at first, Rie is unable to resist Licia's innocent, friendly and loving nature and learns that having a friend isn't so bad after all. The two girls bond through their mutual love of food and through their opposite but also complimentary personalities.
The game has great music, cute and colorful artwork and backgrounds, and features tons of photos of yummy looking food! The photos of the food and ebi-hime's descriptions made me feel really hungry. To read through all of the unique dialogue, it took me about 4 hours in total. There are a total of 5 different endings, a wide variety of gallery art, and also additional things such as: concept art, cut content that never made it into the game, and the writer's thoughts on each character.
Would recommend to those who like a very tame and light hearted VN (no swearing, nudity, etc), and for those who like ebi-hime's other workings.

This review is for the Linux version of the game. I cannot in good concience recommend this game. Don't get me wrong - the game itself is awesome. Unfortunately, the Linux port is not great (or at least, I encountered too many issues to make it worth fixing). First off, there is a bug which freezes you in place every time after a combat sequence. I found two ways to fix this, one (not a good way at all) is to quick save / quick load after every single combat. Second, is to turn v-sinc on or off and reboot the game several times. Now, this wasn't enough to make me rage quit yet. That happened many hours later when my SSD suddenly unmounted itself in the middle of playing, causing the game to crash. I ended up reinstalling the game on my other SSD so I could pick up where I left off (I was using cloud save since I play on both the desktop and laptop pc's) but when I did, it would not let me load (not even get to the loading screen), it just said, 'you have no save games'. So, I tried starting a new game, thinking that I could check the cloud save box that way. The only problem was, doing that somehow caused it to overwrite my previous cloud saves with the new one which was at the beginning of the game! So all the work I did was just gone. Still, I wasn't ready to rage-quit just yet. I decided to be stubborn and see if I could try to hack a save game file to approximate where I was in my destroyed save. There exists an editor for save files, but it only works on Windows. So, I decided to download some save game files from the internet. I successfully loaded them, but unfortunately the person in that playthrough took a different order with things, so it doesn't line up with the way I played through. So now basically if I want to actually enjoy the game, I would be forced to painstakingly crawl through the save game files with a hex editor and figure out about a thousand variables and edit them manually. That would probably take as long (or likely longer) than just starting over from scratch with a new character. But then, there would be no guarantee that something similar would not happen again. So in the end, I am not rage-quitting - I am sad-quitting. Maybe someday some light-side soul will create a save file editor for linux. Until then, if you run linux, do yourself a favor and don't buy the game. Or do buy it, make the editor, and send it to me and I will buy you a beer.

Usually i'm not writing reviews but this hidden gem deserves to have one.
Apotheon is indie 2D action platformer with unique graphics, excellent soundtrack and great story.
Let's look at these aspects a bit closer.
Graphics: When you check the store or screenshots from the game, the most notable part is its beautiful art style. The characters, buildings, weapons, armors, animals, backgrounds- in short everything is like a painting on greek vases.
However it's not all nice and beauty. When you enter the combat be prepared for gore and gruesome parts-specially when you meet Ares.
Soundtrack: Now this is what i talking about. The creator of OST totally nailed the atmosphere of ancient Greece. Each location has unique and fitting theme-desperate whispers in the village of Dion, pompous choir when you enter Olympus, unsettling tunes when you come to Hades, etc. Sometimes you just want to stop and listen this masterpiece.
Story: Apotheon shows us how God of War would looks like if it was 2D. Each Olympian is portrayed like in myths-Hera is jealous, Zeus is angry with humanity and spamming lightning blots, Hades doesn't give a damn what's going on the upper world, Dionysus wants to party hard,etc. Now this is where it get interesting- NOT all gods are utter d☺uchebags. Some have their own agenda, in fact they are willing to help you, unlike GoW where you killing everything in your way without a single thought. If you're new to greek mythology, don't worry- there are lorestones which expain everything-from what kind of god you'll facing, their background story and why they live in such places.
Pros: unique graphics, excellent soundtrack, story, enterntaining fights, huge spectrum of weapons, weapons can break (ok i know it sounds like a con, however this aspect makes you think/ strategize which weapon you'll use against each enemy), huge world to explore
Cons:  some side quest are overly complicated (specially Treasure Hunter and A Hero's Due), clunky controls
Summary: Apotheon isn't just a game, it's artistic experience-from graphics and soundtrack to storytelling. If you're fan of greek mythology, stylish 2d platformer games or you just want to experience something new, this game is just for you.
My final verdict-  9/10 -a great game

Siege also receives eight updates a year. Four updates are balance changes / bug fixes, while the other four are content updates. Usually, these updates are pretty solid, adding new operators to play, new maps to learn, or fixing issues that have been discovered.
It's fairly clear that Ubisoft Montreal truly cares about this game, and wants it to be good, and I think they're doing a pretty darn good job of accomplishing that.
Overall, I'd give it a 8.5/10
