Apotheon has some really good ideas and an excellent art aesthetic, but it fails to establish cohesion with all of its elements. The tutorial teases stealth mechanics and cerebral combat, but the moment you step foot onto Mount Olympus that promise quickly crumbles apart.
The unique feature of controlling the main character, Nikandreos, compared to other Metroidvanias, is that you can precision aim using the right analog stick. The stick locks your aim into its last position, so you can mix jumping with the face buttons and adjusting your aim pretty easily, keeping you from having to claw grip the controller or awkwardly switch back and forth. I can imagine it works pretty well with the keyboard and mouse too. Though the controls are relatively easy to learn and use, it's also slow compared to simply having a predictable attack arc like in other games. Doubling down on this sluggish feeling, every attack you make has a slow windup before it strikes, meaning that you still have to plan on that delay when you're taking this aim. And in addition, the game has a stamina system that makes your attacks even slower if you spam them too much, punishing button mashing. It's a set of mechanics that invites meticulous gameplay focused on accuracy rather than agility, and begs for enemies that are highly telegraphed and just as meticulous as you. Sadly the game's enemies - in general - directly clash with this design, often wildly flying about and flailing their weapons as if they don't follow the same stamina rules that you do. So, I ended up button mashing anyway, and spamming the dodge roll to lure enemies into more favorable positions. This creates a lot of frustrating situations which I bypassed using the trove of consumables I had collected rather than adapting to the situation with my own wit and skill - this is true even when I increased the game difficulty to the maximum allowable.
To make matters worse, the game lacks any input buffering. To describe this issue, I'll use the game's bow. Like all the weapons in this game, you have to slowly draw back your bow, and after you shoot there's a recovery animation afterward in which you are vulnerable. To draw the bow back, you hold down the fire button, and to shoot the bow, you let go of the fire button. However, if you immediately push and hold the fire button after firing - during that recovery animation - the game will not accept your input. Because of this, if you're not paying close attention to Nikandreos' animations (instead of paying attention the enemy's ruthless onslaught), or if you don't figure out the rythm of time you need to wait after firing your bow, you're likely going to feel like the game's controls are simply unresponsive (which is what I thought at first.) Even after I figured it out, it still felt really awkward. There are moments when the system works just fine, and thankfully the game's ending was appropriately epic and satisfying. It's just that, as a whole, the game feels almost broken in its current state.
This charlie foxtrot of design decisions applies to the game's story presentation as well. The story is simple - Zeus is a being a jerk, and his wife Hera is fed up with him not being able to keep it in his pants (I mean, he also doesn't wear any anyway), so Hera has you go up to Mount Olympus and commit deity genocide just to get back at him. With Greek Mythology being such a rich and interesting culture - and having such a great graphical presentation to go with it - this feels like a wasted opportunity. They might as well have had the game open with a Mega Man style stage select with a greek god's face in each box.
Some areas do a better job at introducing the god-to-be-assassinated with its cutscenes, but as a whole I felt like they were just a quarry to be slain. Scattered throughout the game are quotes from actual greek mythology texts, but a lot of them seem tenuously relevant at best. It's a haphazard attempt to stay true to the source material. If they were going to bother with that sort of thing, they could have used one of the many rich stories that already exist in greek mythology and made a video game based on that - it's not like there are already a lot of video games that do that effectively. Instead, you can access Hades from the Olympus sewer system, Zeus just likes to watch the world burn, and you have a game that boils down to awful boss fights with an awkward mess of mechanics.
And I'm not saying that they absolutely had to make it an adaptation for it to be great. There's another game based on an ancient mythology which also adopts an artstyle that mimics ancient paintings - it's called Okami. That game borrows a lot of names and concepts for its events, but it's true to none of its source mythologies. I mean for one, Amaterasu is a shy sun goddess who hid in a cave until she was enticed to emerge by someone gifting her a mirror, not a quirky pun-inspired wolf that urinates on her enemies. The difference is that Okami creates new characters that would hold up in spite of players not knowing anything about the original inspirations. In fact, it creates its own internal mythology as the backdrop for the entire game. Apotheon on the other hand does something awkwardly in between Okami's original-but-inspired approach and adaptation.
In spite of all these complaints, there were moments I was having genuine fun with Apotheon. I actually think they managed to nail rewarding exploration, to the point that even though I dreaded coming across enemies, I still spent the extra time to collect the larger optional finds. For justifying its Metroidvania level design, I can at least award Apotheon with a gold star.
I just really wish everything else came together. The story is passable - it is a video game after all - but if they could pull that combat back to the drawing board and give it a good hard analysis and upgrade, I think Apotheon could be great. In its current state, it's something that I find difficulty recommending.

Pharaoh Rebirth+ is an exciting and creative metroidvania starring an adventuring archaeologist rabbit man and his nerdy sidekick. The game takes place in Egypt and features a wide variety of Egyptian locations, creatures, and folklore for you to encounter.
This game is incredibly well polished for an indie title. The sprite-based graphics are fluid and full of little details, the soundtrack is catchy, and good snappy controls (save for a small exception). There’s loads of attention dedicated to minor things like how certain subweapons work underwater or in heavy winds or the number of cleverly hidden secrets and how to reveal them. The story is really good too and has a few surprises in store for the player as well as a bonus level if you find a certain item.
Despite all the pros I mentioned earlier, this game does have its drawbacks. To start, it’s a bit short and the normal mode plays a bit more like easy mode. I highly recommend starting PR+ in hard difficulty to get the real experience and to try and get the secret level to really get your gameplay’s worth.  Also the mapping system is a bit annoying with how it comes up if you hit up twice and I accidentally triggered it a lot as a result.
All in all, I had an overall positive experience with Pharaoh Rebirth+ even though I had to play it all over again due to a nasty bug (see below) but the game was so good I didn’t even mind. I highly recommend this title to any fan of metroidvanias.
BEWARE: there is a game breaking bug in the 6th stage boss fight. To avoid it: stay near the left side of the area for the entire fight. You may also want to back up your save data file manually just in case.

As a titular assassin your task is to eliminate targets by any means necessary and at all cost - even if it requires sending an air strike on tens of thousands of civilians or planting the bullet in the head of your ally just because he could possibly spill the information.
Your toolkit consists of stealth, knife, multiple ranged weapons and environmental hazards (incineration, electrocution, explosion).
Being a versatile proffesional you can bypass obstacles in numerous ways - either be it a ghost who goes unnoticed till he reaches his target, gunslinger elliminating enemies with bullets, assassin armed with the knife or a butcher running in berserk and slashing humans like pieces of venison. Game itself is stealth focused so open fight is difficult but possible and fun to master, you can even slash armed enemies to death with your knife if you like so. And the character you play do like it - just look at her facial expression when she slits ones throat - this mocking grim of perversive pleasure of taking ones life gives me the creeps.
Controls could be annoying at the beginning. Player could think that developers were lazy and can't give character simple actions like climbing, jumping, crawling etc. but later in the game you see that our heroine is really mobile and can do everything we need but we are forbidden to do so until special situation occurs. Then we can jump between rooftops, jump over the fances, pull up on the crates, climb ladders, crawl under structures and so on. Just the narration of the story limits our actions. Because this game is about narration, not about open world slaughter-fest.
Combat possibilities are nice and as a mixture of stealth, gunplay and enviro-kill are really enjoyable. You can start encounter by blowing some barrels with silenced pistol thus killing one guard with explosion and when others are alarmed and go to investigate you stab one with the knife and finish the last one with the shot in the head with your gun. And when suddenly another one shows up 'out of nowhere' you activate your adrenaline rush, dash to him and puncture to death. Or simply sneak through. It is up tou your taste or score you want to get at the end of the mission.
Every resource in the game requires you to scavenge the map for its replacement - there is no regeneration of adrenaline, health or armor, no basic gun with infinite ammo and you can't even pick up weapons from fallen enemies. Game gives you strict rules how you should play it and let's you enjoy it in a fair manner.
Stealth is really basic, being in the shadow means you are invisible up to really close range. You can move bodies, wear disguise, peek through keyholes and lure enemies with the whistle. Being spotted doesn't mean restart at the checkpoint, you can still take cover, pull out the gun and fight back or use mentioned adrenaline which enables short bullet-time.
AI is solid and enemies, when alerted, will look behind corners and turn around nervously so you can't just make noise in one place and stab them in the back - they will see you if they pass close by, they can turn around at the moment you don't expect and they will wander around looking for the source of noise. In gunfight expect to be flanked so sitting in one spot and waiting for enemies to walk into your crosshair can end up badly unless you have really good camping site.
I'm 7 hours into the game, counter says it's 8th out of 12 missions and I'm curiously looking forward how will it end, but it is already worth its price [regular 5e] so I can honestly recommend it right now.

A lot of good things can be said about Apotheon. It instantly catches the eye with an art style that takes paintings from ancient Greece and brings them to life. Varied boss designs create memorable encounters that are tailored to the mythos of each God. Marios Aristopoulos' dark and powerful soundtrack expertly matches the setting.
Sadly, these highlights are let down by controls that feel floaty and imprecise. I often felt like I was controlling a flailing drunkard, and I'm not referring to the wine drinking challenge of Dionysus. I like some of the concepts they tried to build into combat but the final implementation was rarely satisfying. Additionally, the story fails to be memorable as in never deviates from what you'd expect.
I've wavered back and forth on whether or not to recommend this game. It is far from terrible, but there are many better games out there, particularly if the Metroidvania tag is what attracted you. This is more of a side scrolling action platformer with light map exploration elements. Steam global achievements also show a relatively low completion rate of 11.6% and a pretty heavy drop off between the first story based achievement and subsequent ones.
You'll quickly amass a wide arsenal of weaponry, with some more useful than others. Axes and clubs hit hard but swing slowly. Spears, swords and ranged weapons are more agile but don't pack as much punch.
The fact that only the pointy bits of a weapon can deal damage (E.G. the spear head but not the shaft) could have been cool if the controls allowed me to deftly wield the weapon. Instead, it more often led to wild swings and misses than precision strikes.
I never discovered a way to guarantee a specific swing pattern. In other words, when I hit the attack button I couldn't be sure whether I was going to get a swift thrust or a slow overhead arc. This made timing strikes somewhat of a guessing game.
Shields are also an important part of the game but don't pair well with slower weapons. I can successfully block an attack and then begin swinging my weapon only to be hit by the same enemy's next attack before mine connects.
Weapons and shields have a durability bar that diminishes fairly quickly with use. I'm usually not a fan of durability systems in games but this one encourages you to experiment with new weapons and there's never a shortage of arms.
Switching weapon and potion type in battle is a clumsy experience on a controller. You use the D-pad to scroll through a single, long list of item icons. This makes finding something specific a challenge and for the short lived enhancement potions it rarely felt worth fumbling through this menu to use them. The game's crafting system is hurt by this because all of what you can make are consumables accessed through this interface.
Combat and exploration can drag outside of unique boss encounters and areas. Considering the setting they did a decent job by including as many enemy types as they have. Even still, fighting mostly humanoids does get repetitive.
Unlike many Metroidvanias, Apotheon doesn't have areas that are inaccessible until you get an ability later in the game. Progress is instead limited by simple locked doors. Level design isn't simple, but it is less nuanced with fewer secrets and intertwined areas. As mentioned before, I hesitate to even call it a Metroidvania. It does have a helpful map that is useful for keeping track of where you've been.
There are a handful of neat side quests throughout the game. They reward careful exploration but don't add much to the bigger story.
In closing, I think many people are drawn to Apotheon by its graphics and setting. It's unfortunate then that the developers played the setting so safely that it comes off like they had nothing interesting to add to it.

Where to start... I will start with a rather bold statement. Pyre by Supergiant Games is my "Best Game of 2017". Why? To start this game has fanstatic visuals, each character is unique in both personality and visage. Pyre takes place in such a vibrant and colorful world that this games lore rivals many other stories and worlds created in other games. This game had me completely immersed in the charm and beauty of it's world. In the campaign there are many choices the protagonist makes, and dare I say that the atmosphere created by the story makes every chocie feel important, from causally talking to party members, to make key choices that effect the outcome of the game. You truly feel responsible for everyones freedom and wellbeing. The characaters all have incredibly differing personalities and I feel in love with every single one. Each character is voiced beautifully, and with a flair of foreign language created by the developers it is a expirence that only a true artist could replicate. The gameplay itself is easy to learn, and hard to master. I spent hours in practice mode trying each race and a combination of different competitors. The gameplay is extremely unique, with the sermon's voice leading on the Rite, every battle seems both paramount to your party and that failure is not an option. Pyre's gameplay is both refeshingly different and extremely addicting. I only had one disapointment for this game and it is that there is no online play, which is a damn shame given how immensely fun the gameplay is.
Now for my favorite part of this game. The soundtrack. Each piece of music in this game is a work of art. Not only did Pyre create a musical masterpiece for every occasion, but the had the briliant idea to add an interactible that allows the player to listen to a replication of music that has been heard before in the styling of a minstrel's lute. I spent an hour alone listening to Barker's Theme on repeat.
Overall this game weaves a story like no other, completely unique to everyother title out there. With a price tag of only $21, this game is a steal. I highly recomend this game to anyone with a love for: Fantasic visuals, Musical masterpieces, Briliant world design, Characters you fall in love with within the first two minutes of dailog and Outstanding gameplay. A true 10/10.

Pyre created a very memorable experience for me, as all the other SG games did. After finishing it, I can clearly recall very fond memories of the journey from start to finish, as well as memories of my companions. This is exactly what I'm looking for in single player games - creating a pleasant and memorable experience. For this reason alone, I can recommand Pyre to anyone who is looking for the same thing.
However, there is one thing I disliked quite a lot - the way in which the story is told. In Bastion and Transistor, there is a narator who tells you the most important things which you need to understad the overall story. There was something to read but it was optional. The narration didn't break the flow of the game. I felt like the narration in Pyre was worse.
There is A LOT to read and not all the text is essential for the overall story. You get to read about individual characters, the locations, about your oponents, how everybody feels, etc. There is a lot of flavor text mixed with text which is actually quite important to understand the story. Meanwhile, the 'combat' is actually quite action based. That created this wierd contrast of action based combat and slow pased dialog.
I definitely prefered the narration in Bastion and Transistor, so if that is what you are looking for, this might not be a game for you.

Just downright fun, but maybe for a certain niche?  I grew up watching the Jason movies, as well as Freddy, Michael, and the rest of them.  Jason scared me the most.  The fact that he doesn't run, but can just show up in front of you no matter how hard and far you've run.  The fact that he's a huge brute of a killer who can crush you with his hands or drive a spear all the way through you.  The fact that a hockey mask was a symbol of fear my entire childhood and young adult life.  No other movie franchise has done that to me.
...And now you get to live it through a video game!!  It is faithful to the movies in every way.  The counselors are idiots who trip over themselves and rarely make it out alive.  Jason is an absolute nightmare, but can be stunned and out-witted.  I love all of it, because it's like interacting with the movies.  Maybe if I wasn't such a fan the dynamics of the game would bother me and seem "unfair"... but that's how the movies are, so I expect nothing less.
I started playing it a week after its release date, and I haven't experienced any server issues or bugs or anything as of yet.  Sure the lobby can take a while, but that doesn't spoil the game for me.  It's a good time to grab snacks and a drink!
I'll say it one last time, if you love the movies and always wondered if you had what it takes to escape one alive, you will love this game, because it is totally faithful to the movies.

I genuinely enjoy this game and hope to see it go somewhere eventually. Maybe even potentially getting DLC to add different factions from Knights, Samurai, and Vikings (maybe some things like Romans/Natives. The pool for warrior factions is just massive and I would be delighted to see what they might add). It's a great game, with great graphics and lots of potential. I just have a few quirks with it.
The combat system is AMAZING for one on one combat scenarios, it just makes the duel feel so rewarding for landing hits and great combos. On the other hand though, when thrown into a 4v4 game of Dominion, Deathmatch, or Skirmish, more likely than not you'll find yourself fighting two, or three other people.  Basically making the combat system developed for locking in on one opponent for a perceived as supposed "Honorable" (usually ending with you getting thrown into an environmental for an instant death without even getting hit) is just destroyed.
Another thing I have against it is the fact that Ubisoft made the decision to not implement Dedicated Servers and rather use Peer to Peer networking. NOW, P2P networking has a few games I do enjoy, but for a game like For Honor where the fractions and slightest hundreths of seconds and change you winning or dieing it just doesn't work. You can queue up for a game and it manages to find a full game and come up with a message stating "Unable to connect to game, session is full" which I find interesting the matchmaking will find FULL lobbies and kick you out of queue for them. P2P also allows for the abuse of lag switches, which there are a few tutorials up that can show you how to easily create them which is sad. Because of being P2P you can also be playing and have the host leave, causing you to completely pause the game and halt until it sets up a new host. And sometimes it doesn't even fix it, it just ends up trying to establish a new connection and failing, resulting in you getting kicked out.
My final verdict is: this is a great game, it was hard for me to decide whether to leave a positive or negative review. I finally came down to the decision of a negative review because as the game stands now, the $60 price tag isn't wholely worth it. You will be guaranteed to find a better medieval combat game with dedicated servers for less than $60. I applaud Ubisoft for the effort, but they have managed to go backwards for me in my interest of their games.

This game HAD A LOT of potential, but it lost its way.
here is a quick summary of the good points:

Here are the bad points:

2. New content that gets added isn't very impressive, it no longer sets itself apart from other games liek Day Z like all the reviews initially said.

When I first saw the teasers for this game, I thought it's going to be a Bioshock ripoff. Thankfully, I was totally wrong.
SOMA managed to far exceed my expectations and slowly became one of my favorite videogames of all time.
Take note: This is NOT the kind of horror game that relies on cheap jumpscares to entertain the players. In this regard, SOMA is more like it's predecessor: Amnesia - The Dark Descent. There are only a few encounters with proxies (monsters) and honestly, the game would be nearly as perfect without them as it is with them. Does this mean the game is not scary? Not at all. But you have to look into the story to understand the true creepyness and the dark themes it explores.
The main questions SOMA deals with are: What is it that makes us human?  Can we really draw a line between biological and digital forms of existence?
MINOR SPOILERS AHEAD!
You play as Simon Jarrett, a young man from Toronto, who suddenly finds himself in the abandoned underwater facility of PATHOS-II after having his brain scanned. A mysterious woman named Catherine gets in contact with him through a handheld device called the Omnitool and guides him around on the base.
As he finds out later on, 116 years have passed since his scan and a meteor has obliterated all of Earth's surface.
PATHOS-IIs ARK is the last pillar of humanity's existence, a satellite which contains the digitized consciousness of some residents. Unfortunately, the launch wasn't carried out, thanks to PATHOS' WArden Unit, an artificial intelligence that got out of control and took over the base. The WAU does everything in order to complete it's ultimate task: Preserving human life. However, it seems like the AI's definition of life is anything but ordinary.
Simon decides to help Catherine in launching the ARK, but getting to the satellite is a tough journey, as the WAU's absurd creations roam around decaying facility.
SPOILER ENDS HERE

This is an early access game, I knew that getting involved with it. So I knew the road was going to be bumpy and it still is bumpy and I’m cool with that.
When I first started playing, it was basically a bird bath simulator. It didn’t have any goals, you sat around the watering hole and either sat there or tried to kill each other. No exploring, nothing else to do. That was it. It was boring in the long run. Cool you could run around as a dino, but that was it. The maps even failed to a point, you’d break your leg all the time for how it was set up. It just….it wasn’t the best by any means. The concept of a broken leg is a really fun dynamic to me, but it wasn't working that well with the old maps.
Now though? They have a new map, it’s beautiful. It’s HUGE which right now is kinda a problem because you have 50 players max and you can play for hours without running into anyone period for how massive the map is and the lack of AI right now. As well as the V3 map isn’t finished yet, so there’s that. But again. Early Access, so that’s kinda a no brainer there. Even for the fact it’s not finished it’s a million times better than the old maps. It looks so much better, you don’t break a leg every five minutes and generally speaking you learn the usual spots people gather, like you did with the older maps.
Progression is new, I remember before progression and now we have it, even if it's no where near finished. I think it’s going to turn into a great game mechanic. It is not perfected yet and it isn’t fully implemented so it has some issues, and that in turn leads to frustration. Again, early access. For what they are doing, and what their goals are with progression in making this a survival game. They’re headed in the right direction. I’m really liking the direction they are taking and the challenges they are putting in place to make you actually care if you die. It’s not a EEF(Easy Ego Fluffer) game as I like to call them. It’s not meant to be, it never was and it never will be. I personally love that. It’s what makes it different from a lot of the games out today. When you do achieve something, you have a right to actually feel proud of your achievement.
One thing that was very frustrating is the lack of solid info on where the game is going, like mostly you have to have your questions answered by rumors which isn’t a solid ‘this is how it is’ kind of thing. If you miss a stream you have to hope someone else remembers what was said and even then, you get that lost in translation deal. That seems to be being recently combated now by the updates Dondi has started to do. The August update summary, then the September update summary where he went into some detail on what they are going to be working on. So when I first got the game it was frustrating in knowing what was what, and it’s still going to be very unclear for new people who join the community now on some things. But it’s getting better and as he writes those updates it’ll become easier to know what is what I feel.
The developers are a little rough around the edges but they don’t seem outright spiteful or cruel. So far I have seen that they respond when provoked. So no, the developers are not what they are made out to be by most of the reviews here. When you act like a mature adult and give them the respect you expect in return, they’re easy to talk to. They don’t spend all their time answering every ones questions because they’re working on the game, I’m fine with that personally. I would rather they work on the game then talk to me all the time. Getting to see the live streams is a lot of fun, and it gives you a true appreciation to just how much work it actually is in developing a game. Not every question gets answered or acknowledged when he does his streams. Sometimes I think he misses them in the chat, others I think he purposely refrains from answering to leave mystery to what's to come. Could be wrong but that's how it feels to me.
All in all if you can get past the fact that it’s WIP and things come and go, it has it’s bugs, and players that exploit those bugs make the game…..frustrating currently. Get the game. It’s fun, every day there’s almost a new update to make it work a little better or add a new game mechanic because the developers are actively working on it. Sometimes when one thing works another breaks. I would not recommend getting this if you want a polished game, but if you want to be part of something great, Get this game. This game has tons of potential in becoming one hell of a survival horror game. Yes it’s frustrating, yes it has issues that need fixed, everything is WIP, but that’s what happens when a game is Early Access. Keep that in mind when considering purchasing this game and becoming part of the community.

The bad
Lets just say the new sound update sounds like they recorded it with a 90s mic in the back seat of a car in a back pack... seriously.. nasty sounds. The Garage function is broken.. at least in my case bad. If you edit ANYTHING it will either spawn with no engine or transmission or sometimes the car spawns with no body... idk. strange..(note was fine before update did all the verfiys and even reloaded the game... still broken) Useing a joypad in the gargage function sometimes make it act like its in driving mode and makes the UI unresponsive. The cars physics are.. off? Alot of driving you get the feeling of Light as a feather\driving on ice. I mean some cars you cant even go up a even mild grade in the grass. The good
Its runs pretty decently. Frame rates for me are great. Throttle control and braking are realistic. Gear ratios are accurate and making changes does affect engine performance and rpm based performace this is something alot of games get wrong (ie a l4 gas engine not going to pull like crazy at 2000rpm like a V8 Gas engine would likewise power fades above 4500 in a v8 while power is strong and growing in the L4) things like that are a nice touch (tho the diesels seem to have gas engine characteristics). The Manual gear box options are great with rev matching done automaticly for you. (even tho the sounds are blubbley when this happens maybe the sound is based on rpm?) Adding force induction (Turbos\Superchagers) Makes moddest power gains not these wild gains in other games. Also being able to adjust waste gate timing is nice. It even seems to affect performace but we all know you just love that blow off. I do admit some engine sounds sound amazing! the F1 ish wine of some the trubo l4s is great and the roar of the american V8 is lovely (however idle sounds are way to quite. no lie i would love to have a large cam idle for some of the american v8s) I know these are only of the IN GAME cars stock out of the box i have yet to try other mods as of yet. There are LOTS of options (be it broken ) in tuning the car. (tho.. the engine seems to be runing just fine with this happens....)
Things I would like
Fix the sound please...and the Garage! (maybe its just me..) Window tint... idk just would be nice.. More maps out of the box! A heads up GPS. (idk once again have not played with any mods these are all stock play) A open world sever would be cool with other players (like a GTA ish map set up but that might be asking way to much)
Final Thoughts
Its fun. Worth a play. Worth what they are asking for it. Its early access so yes...its a buggy mess at times. BUT it does work well. Plays decently and...yes..with pactice you to can be driving your AE86 sidways down a mountian listening to Running in the 90's (and crash into a rock because you suck at life)

A decent little platformer. It would be a lot more enjoyable if you weren't stopped every two screens to read a small novel's worth of dialogue.
You ever play a game that has a lot of dialogue in it, and you get the sense that the only reason the dialogue is there is because the developer didn't know that you can make a game -without- dialogue?
Like, take the bit near the end of Sonic & Knuckles, where you have to fight Knuckles (if you're playing Sonic), and then when you beat him Robotnik comes in and swipes the Master Emerald. And then Knuckles opens the secret back entrance for you.
That last sentence alone inspires whole novels of fanfic BUT THE POINT IS! that Sega told a whole little story using just sprite animations. No need for talky boxes. Especially not talky boxes that presented dialogue one sentence at a time, so that by the end of a sequence your thumb has more blisters just from pressing the "Advance dialogue" button than from playing the game itself.
Speaking of, the controls are mostly tight, the level design could use some tweaking (there's a couple of screen transitions where you'll walk right into an enemy if you're not already in the middle of a jump), the music isn't too repetitive, and there are enough save points scattered around to keep things from feeling unfair.

Quick and dirty: YOU can play this game; it's not nearly as hard as it seems. If you want a Metroidvania in an Order of Ecclesia style (focusing on shorter levels with tigther design over progression systems and exploration), this is it. It feels great to play. There's a lotta room for player expression with subweapon use. Weirdly engaging plot. But it's a bit of a hesitant recommendation. It's definitely worth the normal asking price, though. If you want it, get it whenever.
Its controls are tight, but not corset-tight (particularly, 1) playing with a joystick causes some awkward hiccups; diagonals are interpreted as 2 keyboard keys; this causes issues with reading signs mid-jump or misalligning shots with a certain weapon, 2) the edges of platforms are almost TOO accurate to the architecture, yet your character's "feet" for determining collision with the ground are smaller than the sprite's).
The Metroidvania progression feels reeeeally forced and hoakey. These aren't gimmicks that get you to look at levels in new lights; there are obvious barriers to progress to single, empty rooms with singular power up items. If you try to go back each time you get a progress power-up, you'll be disappointed. Only breaking boxes and double jumping give you new, fun challenges.
The looser Metroidvania structure also hurts it as an action-platformer. It feels as if checkpoint placement wasn't considered in a non-linear fashion; this is most obvious in Stage 4, where the placement of enemies along slow, elevator-like grapple chains assumes a vertical or downward ascent based on an optimal level route that isn't clear until completion.
The game can be suddenly punishing (mine cart level, ahoy!), especially with its long GAME OVER screen, but the lack of difficulty makes a game bursting with personality play like a vanilla wafer. There are many mechanics which are interesting but never required or dramatically helpful. You get a massive iinvincibility-frame dash, an aerial attack that pushes you back up slightly in the air, etc.--but there are no segments that force you to use the dash or platforming using this unique mechanic. If anything, their use trivializes much of the stage and boss design. You CAN finesse boss fights, but brute-forcing them is just as effective.
A lot of the bosses have amazing, well thought-out, varied patterns that interact in surprising ways with your arsenal of subweapons... but you can easily just eat 1 carrot per bossfight (makes you invincible for 10+ seconds and ups your attack power), use your i-frame dash to cheese through their attacks that punish you for staying at close range once it wears off, and rush them down. The reward for succesfully figuring out good sub-weapons to use is often not the difference between survival and defeat, but seeing much less of a great boss than it feels you should.
It's a game that's less than the sum of its parts. But, it's still neat as hell.
The aesthetics are on point. The music has an emotional breadth while never failing to raise intrigue in cutscenes or keep you pumped up during levels. The sprites are GORGEOUS--please, play this in windowed mode if you can't get this to scale by whole numbers in fullscreen. Some of the use of paralax bakgrounds and varying visual styles among enemies and bakgrounds--it's this wonderful mash of strict depiction and heavy abstraction at once (just see the main character set up against beautiful, lineless backdrops of palm-trees and the ocean's horizon line).
And there are some real feats of creative game design--particularly, check out how the machine gun interacts with chokepoints in the environment or how much enemy interaction changes once you consider the claymore in stage 4... but much of it is just an unchallenging, decompressed action platformer that saves its flair for boss fights and laaate game optional rooms, leaving a lot of unimpressive downtime.
Oh, and the story?? Is excellent?? Reminds me of when movies took queues from movies but didn't try to be them--it has punchy little asides between action segments to progress the plot with laugh-out-loud dialogue. Unintrusive and compelling.

So what makes Bejeweled
? If you've ever played their games, you know there's nothing more satisfying than matching chains of gems and watching them explode dazzingly. Now, you get to have three times the explosion in Bejeweled 3!
In the third sequel of Bejeweled, new game modes were added which introduces various mechanics and playstyles. They can range from adrenaline-pumping maps that require your swift reactions, to mind-bending puzzles that puts your gem-matching strategy to the test. Of course, old school bejewelers can still have fun racking up their scores in the original Classic mode. However, if you prefer something more relaxing, the Zen mode features an endless tile map coupled with soothing atmospheric soundtracks.
If you're a fan of match-3 games, Bejeweled 3 is undoubtedly a great addition to your game list. If you're curious about the game and looking forward to buy it on a sale, try it out! It's always fun to watch your gem formations explode, whether if you do it with careful planning or with a relentless matching blitz.

Strawberry Vinegar is fairly short, taking only a few hours to reach the good ends.  While not long, it is stuffed full of beautiful art, cute characters, delicious food, and good feels.  I caught some bad ends early on and while that could have been frustrating under most circumstances, the way they were delivered made me realize that I had to think about how my character would act for each choice, as a gloomy reclusive 9-year-old girl.  That realization helped me feel more invested in the characters and in guiding them well.
The CG art is beautiful and plentiful, featuring some of the most beautiful hand-drawn renders I have seen.  The character sprites are expressive and varied.  The music, while it doesn't stand out, suits the scenes and events perfectly.  The characters themselves are interesting and engaging, although they may not be as easy to identify with for someone not familiar with anime tropes.
I chose to play one game "day" per real day.  This made the individual play sessions no more than an hour, but each day as work wound down I found myself looking forward to getting home so I could play again.  I do strongly recommend this game.
However, despite the high production values, at a release price of 10USD I feel the game would be better served listing a few dollars cheaper, due to its brevity.  My second recommendation is to wishlist the game, and buy it as soon as it receives a discount, because the experience it delivers really is very very good.

I found this game incredibly boring, I hated the combat, could care less about the story, and it was far too easy (even on the hardest mode). I would BARELY call this game a metrovania, but if I did, it would be the worst metrovania I've ever played. More just a 2d platformer fighter, I guess.
When I invest my time in a game, I tend to finish them. About an hour into the game I made the choice to not quit as as I had read from other comments that the boss fights were neat. I call BS on that.
The combat of the game was trying to go the same route as dark souls, but fell flat on its face. The hit box mechanic was clunky as hell. Weapon breakage was just plain annoying, especially since you could usually only carry one of a weapon at a time. Switching through weapons was a MAJOR PITA (maybe cause I was using a controller?), especially during combat, as the list is long and slow to get through. I ended up in most boss fights just pausing and going to the menu's inventory when i needed to drink a potion or switch a weapon. I probably should have just broken all the weapons I didn't want to use to get them out of my inventory, but then again I probably would have just picked them up again later and had to repeat the process. It would have made a lot more sense for the game to have weapon slots so you could store multiple of your favorite weapons. It really could have taken a page from Breath of the Wild. Also, a large amount of the time when trying to use a potion through the potion-button, it ended up using the wrong one.
I was trying to figure out during the entire playthrough how the hell weapons decided on when to break, until about 75% of the way through the game I finally noticed the little bar under the weapons. I'm usually not one to say tutorials are needed from a game, showing you how they work, but this game is so unintuitive with such a horrible GUI, it would have been really nice for just a 10 second tutorial pointing out the parts of the interface.
The style of the game was neat.. for about an hour, and then just got incredibly repetative. Maybe there was some intereresting stuff there for greek myth fans, but just placing passages from the Iliad and Odyssey in random places doesn't do much for me.
The one good thing I could say about it is there were one or two neat levels. Save yourself the wasted time and skip this one.

It's a TON of fun for the first while. You usually get Jason a lot in your first day or so playing, and fighting him is fun during that time to.
But then you get Jason less and less and less, until you're basically a survivor every time. And when you DO get Jason, the game's true issues start in.
People leaving, the game crashing, etc. the one time you get to be Jason blows. I'd rather que up as Jason and wait 20 minutes than constantly get lobbies where I'm a survivor with a 1/5 chance of Jason killing me before I can get/find anything. 1/5 since at least 2 people probably left already.
There's only three maps and two are basically the same. For the first 10 hours you're fine since spawns are ALWAYS different, but after a while you recognize each individual house on the map and know where every drawer is. It gets old too quickly, which is a shame was when it was new it was truly a blast.
The game can actually be very scary, with the music and atmosphere, I wont deny screaming one time. This was a surprise to me as I expected a silly A symmetrical multiplayer wank fest, which I still got a lot of, but the game can definitely and does definitely work as horror.
And as said about the game's issues.. animation issues, some texture issues, bugged houses showing survivors in them when there aren't any, the game crashing randomly when you use shift as Jason, etc.
And 7/10 lobbies you get put into has every player at 200+ ping.. how does that work?
It's a really fun game for a while with serious potential, but not worth the price tag and not worth the current state, unless it's the only state, which case still not worth the price.
tl;dr if you're okay with $40 for about 10 hours of interesting fun in a multiplayer match, sure. If you expect longevity or like games without any bugs, no!

Sniper Elite V2 is a decent sniper game set in World War II.
The campaign features a solid storyline. It is set in 1945 at the close of WWII and you are behind enemy lines trying to stop the launch of the V2 rockets. The campaign packs some fun elements that not only allow you to attack the Germans but also the Russians, which in itself creates an interesting dynamic where alliances do not matter. The game is around six hours long and some missions are obviously more engaging than others. For the most part, the game emphasises freedom in how to engage your objectives and this allows you to go loud or stealth, creating a fun and exciting balance in gameplay. At only six hours in length, the campaign dragged but it did somewhat allow me to invest into the story.
The gameplay is good. It is identical to Sniper Elite 1. The freedom in approach to your missions are interesting in creating strategies on how to engage your enemies without alerting the rest. The gameplay incorporates a slow-motion bullet cam that is now a main part of the Sniper Elite series. It happens so often though that it feels like something to help expand the length of the campaign. The enemy AI is above-average. The machine gunners are smart in listening and knowing where to shoot but the enemy snipers are plain stupid.
I did not play multiplayer. I played this around the time Sniper Elite III was out.
The performence is atrocious. This game does not have much spec requirements and my computer has better specs than the recommnended. I played on low settings with the majority of settings set to off and that was the only chance I could obtain a consistent 60 FPS. Absolutely awful.
Pros:
- Sniping mechanics.
- Freedom in missions.
- AI was somewhat challenging.
Cons:
- Performence.
- Length and quality of campaign. At six hours, the campaign dragged in the final two.
- Enemy Sniping AI.
- A lot of bugs.
Overall, Sniper Elite V2 is a decent game. It features a solid campaign that is interesting enough until it drags. It incorporates fun gameplay with some twists into the strategic element, and will keep you entertained for a few hours. I recommend this on sale. 6.5/10

This is an early access game, I knew that getting involved with it. So I knew the road was going to be bumpy and it still is bumpy and I’m cool with that.
When I first started playing, it was basically a bird bath simulator. It didn’t have any goals, you sat around the watering hole and either sat there or tried to kill each other. No exploring, nothing else to do. That was it. It was boring in the long run. Cool you could run around as a dino, but that was it. The maps even failed to a point, you’d break your leg all the time for how it was set up. It just….it wasn’t the best by any means. The concept of a broken leg is a really fun dynamic to me, but it wasn't working that well with the old maps.
Now though? They have a new map, it’s beautiful. It’s HUGE which right now is kinda a problem because you have 50 players max and you can play for hours without running into anyone period for how massive the map is and the lack of AI right now. As well as the V3 map isn’t finished yet, so there’s that. But again. Early Access, so that’s kinda a no brainer there. Even for the fact it’s not finished it’s a million times better than the old maps. It looks so much better, you don’t break a leg every five minutes and generally speaking you learn the usual spots people gather, like you did with the older maps.
Progression is new, I remember before progression and now we have it, even if it's no where near finished. I think it’s going to turn into a great game mechanic. It is not perfected yet and it isn’t fully implemented so it has some issues, and that in turn leads to frustration. Again, early access. For what they are doing, and what their goals are with progression in making this a survival game. They’re headed in the right direction. I’m really liking the direction they are taking and the challenges they are putting in place to make you actually care if you die. It’s not a EEF(Easy Ego Fluffer) game as I like to call them. It’s not meant to be, it never was and it never will be. I personally love that. It’s what makes it different from a lot of the games out today. When you do achieve something, you have a right to actually feel proud of your achievement.
One thing that was very frustrating is the lack of solid info on where the game is going, like mostly you have to have your questions answered by rumors which isn’t a solid ‘this is how it is’ kind of thing. If you miss a stream you have to hope someone else remembers what was said and even then, you get that lost in translation deal. That seems to be being recently combated now by the updates Dondi has started to do. The August update summary, then the September update summary where he went into some detail on what they are going to be working on. So when I first got the game it was frustrating in knowing what was what, and it’s still going to be very unclear for new people who join the community now on some things. But it’s getting better and as he writes those updates it’ll become easier to know what is what I feel.
The developers are a little rough around the edges but they don’t seem outright spiteful or cruel. So far I have seen that they respond when provoked. So no, the developers are not what they are made out to be by most of the reviews here. When you act like a mature adult and give them the respect you expect in return, they’re easy to talk to. They don’t spend all their time answering every ones questions because they’re working on the game, I’m fine with that personally. I would rather they work on the game then talk to me all the time. Getting to see the live streams is a lot of fun, and it gives you a true appreciation to just how much work it actually is in developing a game. Not every question gets answered or acknowledged when he does his streams. Sometimes I think he misses them in the chat, others I think he purposely refrains from answering to leave mystery to what's to come. Could be wrong but that's how it feels to me.
All in all if you can get past the fact that it’s WIP and things come and go, it has it’s bugs, and players that exploit those bugs make the game…..frustrating currently. Get the game. It’s fun, every day there’s almost a new update to make it work a little better or add a new game mechanic because the developers are actively working on it. Sometimes when one thing works another breaks. I would not recommend getting this if you want a polished game, but if you want to be part of something great, Get this game. This game has tons of potential in becoming one hell of a survival horror game. Yes it’s frustrating, yes it has issues that need fixed, everything is WIP, but that’s what happens when a game is Early Access. Keep that in mind when considering purchasing this game and becoming part of the community.

I won't lie. I was skeptical about Doom. I thought it was a piece of nostalgia that was rated to highly because it was old. But I can say confidently that this game is FUN AS HELL (pardon the pun). How do you describe Doom? Well, I can try. You shoot things. And by god is it fun. Like, (un)holy♥♥♥♥♥♥it's fun. You run through different levels shooting baddies that are either people or demons from hell! You may be thinking that this game is just pixelated COD or something. Well it isn't. I cannot express the grin on my face when I picked up the gatling gun or the rocket launcher. The adrenaline that went through me when I mowed down demons while keeping a close eye on my health. But most people have heard about how great Doom was. You want to know if it holds up. And it does. Each level is expertly designed to make you think about which  way to go. The combat is fast paced and satisfying. The gore is charming in that old fashioned way. The difficulty is nothing to laugh at to. Do you want to feel genuinely terrified that each step may lead into the jaws of an angry demon? Do you want to curse at every missed shot and scour for ammo hoping to find enough bullets to fight off the demons chasing you? Remember, this was in the 90s. Back then, their easy was our hardcore. Everything was difficult as hell (there it is again). And Nightmare on Doom was grueling even by their standards. Every moment while in combat is pure and utter fun. Every baddie slain is like a scene form Fury Road. Now does it have it's flaws? Of course. Plenty. The movement feels very strange at times, some of the controls are questionable and it can't tab out. But these are all flaws inherent with age. This was back when computers ran on DOS. It's going to have a few difficulties when running on a platform that was the ♥♥♥♥ing future when it was released. Windows 10 belonged only in Back To The Future. But strangely enough, it runs beautifully performance wise. Better than most games infact. It's only 5$ too. There is very little reason not to buy this if you are not a fan of gaming. It's a staple. It's up there with Wolfenstein, Mario and Tetris. It's a classic. It's DOOM.

The great:  Originality seeps from every pore of this game.  The artwork is phenominal, the level design is smart, and the music is lively and joyous.  Every character is quirky and fun, even if they're not that different gameplay-wise.  Rayman Legends capitalizes on the simplicity of the platforming genre, and does it in an accessible, streamlined experience.
The good:  The game modes.  When you finally exhaust the immense amount of levels, there is still more to do.  You can play a surprisingly intense round of Kung Foot, which is soccer meets the Matrix.  You can play some levels from the previous games.  You can also do some challenges that are devilishly tricky.  Obviously, this stuff was added as an afterhtought, and it isn't as fleshed out as the main levels, but it was a smart afterthought, because it is still quite fun.
The bad:  It's an Ubisoft game for PC, so you know what that means.  Yup, you're gonna have to deal with the annoyance of Uplay.  Booting up the game from Steam only to have it open Uplay and update itself, and then slowly clunk you into what you actually wanted to do in the first place, which is play the game.  It's unfortunate that this exists, because the developers had nothing to do with this decision and it's all Ubisoft's fault.  Bah humbug.
Overall, this is a must own for lovers of local co-op and/or platformers.  It has a unique charm about it that is unseen elsewhere, and it's worth dealing with Ubisoft's incompetence to get to the reward of this phenominal experience.
Verdict:  Buy it for any price, you won't be sorry.

If you buy this, or any of the other classic DOOM games, you have 2 options to have a decent experience:
1: Get the .WAD files and use them with a source port of your choice, however this wont track your stats on steam.
2: Put a source port in the game directory and rename the source port exe to 'dosbox.exe' and delete the original dosbox of course. This will let you run a source port and still have Steam track game time and show when you're playing it.
Don't even bother using the DOSbox emulation that comes with it, it has performance issues, runs in an awful resolution, has awful sound emulation, and has no mouse look option whatsoever, if you plan on playing it 100% faithful to the original DOS experience, don't use DOSbox, build or buy a 486.

I seriously want to like this game. It has such massive potential.
Pros:
1) Sound is amazing. Play with a good headset and you will be able to hear every footstep and gunshot in beautiful deafening glory. Their sound guy deserves a raise.
2) Bullets hurt. No shrugging off 7.62 rounds like BBs. When you get hit you feel it. Head shot auto-kills, sniper rifles kill with torso shots, unless your carrying heavy armor.
3) Bleeding. When you get shot you tend to bleed, and left untended you will bleed out and die, so if you just winged a soldier as he ran in a building he might fall over dead in a few seconds. Bad part is you medkits to deal with it and they are one use and instant apply. Beginning you will not even know how to use it. When you do, it disappears and then next scratch and you're doomed. There are no ways to get more in game, until you die. Would like to see a medkit be infinity use but you have to hide and spend a several seconds bandaging and or tourniquet. They are so mandatory you will never get to equip any other items, like grenades.
4) Brings back tactics like sneaking and teamwork. At the moment no one works as a team, but if you get a group and do you can seriously dominate. Communication is god. Plenty of cover and concealment for the like minded sniper.
5) Leveling system is awesome idea and can help you specialize your play style, but still needs more work.
Cons:
1) Team Killing Rampant-There is currently no puishment for Team Killing and it happens alot. Nothing you can do about it. Vostek says to take a screen shot and then go to support page and submit evidence, except you can't. Page wont open, can't write a support ticket either, says I dont have permission.
2) Massive Unbalancing, this is one of the most unbalanced games I've ever played. SMG's do everything better than everything else. Get in a game 95% of players using one. Sniper Rifles have no scopes or anything terrible rechambering, slow you down, small mags, and server side glitched will mean you miss alot of shots due to everyone being Nightcrawler all over the map, so its like playing the game on hard mode.
3) Hit Registration is awful often disregarding single shots so sorry again, snipers you will often shoot right through your target while he blows you away with 30 well aimed non-scattering shots. Glitches a plenty fall through map, people teleporting, and invisible players.
4) No safe spawn point. The entire map is open for everyone so if you sneak around the lines, which is easy due to map size and cover, you can just sit in their spawn and kill them as they spawn. This one I can guarentee will happen in every game.
5) No prone. In Future Russia laying on the ground is prohibited, which really hurts snipers, causing you to stand still like a big dumb target.
6) Matchmaking is broken, only game mode you can get into is TDM and you will get matched with players from all tiers of play, so your first game will proabably be against god-tier players with heavy armor and LMG's and the worlds more accurate SMG's ever made. Using weapons that you can no longer attain due to changes in the game. So they will always have an edge over you.
7) In game store. This game has an In game store, which is perfectly fine for a F2P game, except that it is not finished and they say they can't even get small things like the damn "Stars and Stripes" in the game (While they have like 30-40 others and their coat of arms, including even a Atlas has never heard of), but you bet they want you to spend your money on it. Also leveling up without "Premium" is awful. I got no good drops after games, got a few days premium to see the difference, and I got like 10 weapons in one day. You will almost never see one without it.
In this state I cannot recommend this game. That being said, I would love to come back and play this game if they ever fix it. In it's current state it's really a open alpha, with a In Game Store. I do not recommend supporting these shady business tactics in Video Games. Vostek Games please fix yourself please.

TLDR: Ultimately, it’s a decent title for maybe 5 dollars?
First off, let's get the "but you played 55.6 hours". I leave my computer running 24/7, and some times that means a game as well, but even still, the game is BRUTALLY tedious, so even getting one playthrough to a good enough state to say you've seen it all is going to take a reasonable amount of time... but was it worth it?
Let's go through the basics. Right away the UI is horrendous, one of the worst I have ever seen in a game. Is it as convoluted as some text base games? No, but for such a simple game to get it this wrong puts some serious questions in the developer’s court in terms of "do they know what they are doing at all".
UI Sins:
- There’s virtually no options, and no direction on controls save the tutorial.
- Movement is done with the same mouse button as selecting, and the hit box on selecting a character is awful. Movement actions are queued, so to stop moving a character you can't just click another move, you have to cancel the currently queued action. This can create a cluster ♥♥♥♥ of you trying to select a character, move another character trying to stop the first mistake, and so on. I am not even aware of a reason other than shelter invasion where movement even matters. Was it this difficult to make right click move like virtually every other game?
- Consistency is also a problem as right button is reserved for accessing actions available on an object by a character (context menu), but in the expedition preparation window, left click is the context window. Once you learned one backwards command system, throw it out the door.
- Status alerts on needs don't really communicate anything. They fill up, and all look the same, but only start to do something when enough of them are red (still not clear on this as it’s never been a factor even on the most difficult of settings). Some statuses like food and water sometimes confer conditions if left high for too long, but I don't know what triggers "too long". Having to take a♥♥♥♥♥♥= hungry = dirty = tired = thirsty as far as the UI is concerned.
- Getting info on characters like stats, statuses and strengths/weaknesses is virtually impossible after the info popped up on the screen. What xp is doing I also have no idea.
And it’s not just the UI that’s confusing, the mechanics also don't make sense.
- There are tons of perks and mechanics around how fast you do things, but you will spend days sitting around doing nothing. Efficiency of action is barely at play here where it is normally a mainstay of the management genre. You still need to be efficient with resources though...
-Water is used for everything, and if you run out can literally lock you in your shelter. It's so crippling to be without it that almost EVERY OTHER ASSET OR NEED FULFILLMENT IS SUBORDINATE TO IT. After coming back to the game to see what had changed and starting a game on hard, I really started to consider exactly what I needed to play when water was the key thing being limited. I found pretty much the only thing you are going to be building with the first bench is a water butt and some beds. That’s it. Why a toilet when it uses water? A shower is almost unthinkable with the amount of water it uses when the penalty for not showering is make your survivors throw up after a meal (lower’s your action efficiency as you take a break to boot and rally, which as discussed above, means virtually nothing). Honestly the retching sounds is about the only reason to build an early shower.
-There is a ticker on each salvage location that keeps track of time since last visit, but we are never really aware of how long between visits you should wait for resources to re-pop. You can go back even a few days later to a location for as far as I can tell. This system doesn’t make sense or communicate what you are actually supposed to be doing (which is dry humping the same spots every 2-3 days).
Once you penetrate the confusing, you are left with a brutally shallow collection of semi-working concepts:
Never use water for anything but drinking and travel. You won’t be building anything really for the first bajillion days except for butts, beds and more bunker until you collect enough REDICULOUSLY hard to find resources to upgrade your bench. Nearly every other object uses either a rare resource that you need for an upgrade, or solves a problem you don’t need solved at the cost of water to use. I don’t think, even with a heavy first play session, that you will upgrade anything. I would say you might be ready at the end of your second sit-down if you are lucky.
That means you are literally doing nothing but pulling a one-armed bandit that takes water for currency in the hopes to get rope and leather while watching 2 or 3 members idle about vomiting and occasionally mopping (which thankfully takes no water). If you are additionally unlucky you will also be sitting around holding shift down until it rains listening to all 4 members idle and vomit. Your little cardboard box will be full to the brim, since you can't use anything crafting, and 90% of the stuff you bring back will just be discard outside the entrance to your bunker because you need a box to put♥♥♥♥♥♥in and its harder to build than an entire new room of your bunker. Most likely you will have a run in with bleeding your first play through and, satan willing, it will be right after you get your last rope/leather you need to experience anything else.

Honestly, I wasn't expecting much when I bought this game. The screenshots and trailer didn't do much for me, but the gifs on the developer's Twitter page
got me interested. The 'behind the scenes' of the game looked so cool! So, based on the quality of those gifs, I bought the game...and I'm SO glad I did. 'Pharaoh Rebirth +' is an exceptionally well made game with a lot of heart. It's also SUPER fun to play. :)
PROS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
- Likable and well-written characters. I was surprised how much I cared for the characters in this game. Everyone is just so likable and fleshed out. VERY cute and funny dialogue throughout.
- Excellent gameplay. The game runs at a smooth 60 FPS and feels very responsive. LOTS of polish in gameplay overall. Very well done.
- Fun abilities. This is a big one. This is a video game that is not afraid to have fun being a video game. (Following is a minor spoiler) One of the abilities allows you to change your ears into a paper airplane to glide across wide gaps. That right there should tell you everything you need to know. It's silly, it's funny, it's unconventional and it was ALWAYS very fun to play. :)
- There's a metroidvania element, with abilities allowing you to access areas you couldn't previously. However, it has a level-based structure, instead of one big map. This is actually really cool, since it allowed you to just go back to the level where you remember an element was and explore more in that area.
- GREAT music. It's so good. The soundtrack is on my computer right now. LOVE the music SO MUCH!!
- When it was over, I got kinda bummed out since I wanted more to play. That (to me) is always a sign of a great game. I've put 12 hours into the game, beaten it - and still go back quite often to play levels. It's just FUN to play.
- LOTS of abilities and collectibles. If you like to play with new, interesting abilities and find cool collectibles, you'll love this game. ^_^
CONS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
- There are a couple times where the main gameplay is not platforming. Like, they'll have mini-games, puzzles, driving sections and things like that. While I understand that those sections were there to provide variety, they were also my least liked sections of this game. This game EXCELS in platforming, so I just wanted to spend more time doing that. It didn't feel good to get stuck on a section that gameplay-wise didn't have anything to do with the rest of the game. Thankfully, these moments were brief. Just thought I'd mention them here.
- I hear that this game launched kinda rough in regards to vsync support and things like that. I think the devs have pretty much fixed all those issues. Again, just mentioning it.
- The analog controls didn't seem to work 100% of the time for me. The devs patched in a deadzone option, but even with it at the max setting, my character still drifts to the left sometimes. Thus, I ended up playing it with the D-Pad (as opposed to the left analog stick) on a wired Xbox 360 controller. That solved the problem.
OVERALL
---------------------------------------------------------------------
'Pharaoh Rebirth +' is a fantastic game with a lot of heart. Though there were initially a few technical hangups, the fun of the game overcame those shortcomings and I had a BLAST with this game. SO much fun. Very much looking forward to what the devs work on next! :)
P.S. If you want to see another game that the devs have worked on, you can check out 'Action Mogura'. It's available for free online! :) A bit of warning, though: It's only in Japanese and MUCH more difficult than 'Pharaoh Rebirth +'. I beat it in a few days, though - so it's quite playable. Just letting you know. ^_^
FINAL SCORE
---------------------------------------------------------------------
9 out of 10

There needs to be a "Maybe" option for games like this one.
While I do recommend this game, it comes with some stipulations:
1. It must be $5 or less.
2. You must LOVE FPS games.
3. You must understand while the game itself is meh to ok, you're really coming to laugh at the story and dialogue.
You know those films where the dialog and acting are so bad, it becomes entertaining in a funny way? This is the video game version of that.
Summing up the game play:
-The levels are designed well enough and varied, but VERY linear and there's a very noticeable lack of detail at times.
-Enemies aren't varied at all. It's all enemy soldiers and three versions of robots.
-Standard weapons: Pistol, Shotgun, Sniper Rifle, Machine gun, Rocket Launcher, grenades, etc.
-The enemy AI goes from being completely unaware that you're standing in front of them to being able to see your movement through walls and rock.
-Don't waste health because the enemy doesn't miss. Ever. Ok, the guys with the rocket launchers will miss, and the shotgun weilding baddies lack range, but the guys firing pistols and machine guns will always hit you.
-A Max Payne bullet time like system that felt like it wasn't fleshed out. It can help even out the bigger fights agains the enemies who don't miss.
-A driving section that comes out of nowhere with poor driving physics.
-A hacking skill that seems like an after thought, and could have been used more effectively.
The game itself would be kind of bland without the amazingly bad dialogue and voice acting. Don't worry, you'll get the jist of the story. It's just that you're playing a Sci-Fi game with dialogue that's like it's from a bad 1930s crime novel. On top of that, it's read by people who got bad scripts or don't understand punctuation. I'll grant you something might have been lost in translation, but those English voice actors should have known better.
Again, if those three stipulations are things you can deal with, pick it up. If not, you should skip this game.

The ending gave me chills, and the boss fight with Poseidon really felt like I was fighting a god. The music is incredible, and really captures a sense of mystery.
I also love the dialogue. The writing really feels like how Greek gods would actually talk, and the excerpts from actual Greek mythology scattered around the world went a long way to fleshing out the fantasy. It's incredible how much emotion good writing, voice acting, and character design can give to figures with no facial animation. I felt genuine emotional attachments to poor Helios and Daphne for how cruelly Apollo had abused them, and taking revenge on their behalf felt
.
The statues in the background randomly stepping into the foreground  to fight me never stopped scaring me, and the overall atmosphere is superb.
But overall, this game's design doesn't live up to the hype I felt when I saw its unique and brilliant Greek vase art design. The combat is clunky, weapons degrade too quickly, the boss fight with Artemis was a rank disappointment, Athena's lair was frustrating and boring, and there aren't enough non-boss character designs to stop the game feeling monotonous.
But still, this was clearly a work of passion, and the end product is something a pleb like me could never dream of adequately creating. Bravo, AlienTrap!

They both get to know each other, first they start to hate each other, but later in the VN, they start to love each other and show affection to each other. I mean, it even gets to the point where you think a Yuri scene is about to pop up any moment….I mean there are some that do, so don’t be disappointed
If you have read the Visual Novels’ Asphyxia and/or The Sad Story of Emmeline Burns you might be familiar with the graphics, as they are made by the same people. The artwork really shows bright images of the girls and the environment they’re in, they did a great job in terms of the visuals in this novel. The drawing of the girls doesn’t really follow the same “anime-like” appearance as other VNs, which felt unique in its own way, but it also felt “out of place” for me as I wasn’t quite used to it at the beginning.
But overall it delivers a nice artwork for the characters and the environment, great job on this one.
I have already mentioned some of it above. But in terms of “in depth story” it doesn’t go far and long, in fact this VN has really fast pacing and really quick character development, so if you wanted a long, in depth story VN, sadly this is not for you. But for the others, it delivers a nice empathises on both of the girls as they go on about their day. Also, to mention
made her first friend EVER! In her life, that is of course the demon she met, who broke into her home and started eating cookies…well, I guess you can also make friends that way huh, who would’ve thought.
Overall, the novel shows us a story of two girls who show love and affection to each other as the VN progresses on and it portrays their everyday life and show their own personal character development.
Nothing of the amazing to hear in this novel, there is only ever so many soundtracks until you start hearing the same ones that you heard 2-3 scenes ago. However, some are really nicely done, but I wouldn’t say all of them are of “high quality” though. Some of the soundtracks don’t even fit particular scenes, but eh, what can you do?
Overall, the soundtrack is quite a let-down. It doesn’t offer much for the reader as some don’t even match the scene.
The VN offers the basic options in the menu which could alterate your VN experience. It at least has the SHIFT + TAB overlay support which I really liked, but it only worked when you had a high enough frame rate (Between 30-60 FPS), otherwise it wouldn’t function, or sometimes it would work, but it would lag the game or lag the overlay.
Overall, it only offers basic options and gameplay aspects. But this is enough for this kind of VN.
At £6.99 this is a great price for this VN. Any higher than £10 would not have been worth buying at all. This is great to see as many VNs of this length are overpriced despite offering the same features, I’ll give this VN full marks here.
Overall at the price, you get what you pay for, it’s not too low or too high. This is a great price point for this VN.
It is a decent VN with good artworks and a taste of Yuri. That is all I can say for that one. I can only recommend the VN if you are into fast paced stories, cute girls and VNs in general. This is NOT for the “serious” reader if you know what I mean.
