Pyre holds some of the signature SuperGiant elements: the stylelized art, custom soundtrack composed throughout the design process, and rich character and world lore. How these elements fit together in Pyre, however, is different than in Bastion and Transitor.
Who you are in the games:
In, Bastion and Transistor, you follwed of the main character, watched how they interacted with their enemies and environments, but they were not "you." They were their own characters that enacted their own agency at certain moments. E.g. when Red interacts with certain computer modules and when the Kid carries out your decision (trying to be spoiler free). In contrast in Pyre, while some background story is placed onto you, through the dialog trees you have more power over who The Reader is than in other games. Indeed, you don't even know what The Reader looks like; the Reader's silhouette is only revealed in the end credits.  In Pyre, you *are* The Reader.
Where you are:
You and the rest of the exiles are cast away into this horrid wasteland. Should you choose to read the book, you will learn details about how awful the weather, food, and diseases are. Otherwise, you are usually staring at the sky, watching your comrades in the Rites (the 'game' portion of the game), inside the wagon, or watching the wage traverse the vast landscape.  You never zoom in to interact with the lands or watch a cutscene. Except for the brief panorama before the rites, you get a very bird-eye perspective of the place.  When you watch the wagon plant itself or trolly across the lands, it feels as if you are watching your monopoly piece travelling to its next position. While one can appreciate that the whimsical animations of the wagon give it a character of its own, you feel rather distant from the whole settings. You've read that the wasteland is awful, but it really only affects your comrades, not yourself. (Indeed, some shall suffer status ailments due to the settings.) But these ailments have no affect on you at all.  You keep hearing how awful the wasteland is, but since you never experience the game before exile, what are you missing? You, The Reader, may often feel like you are just watching these events unfold. Unlike in Bastion and Transistor where you may have felt like you were *in* those worlds, shaping them, interacting with them. In Pyre, I felt almost like I was watching through a looking glass. In a sense, I was. The Reader  seemed to have no real physical presence in the game except for the opening moments when the masked man feeds and nurses you back to health.
Who you are with:
You travel with a group of Exiles who wish to be free, and you are helping them. They are very accomodating, trusting, and provide levity to an otherwise dreary situation. In contrast, many of the adversaries you face, while still interesting in character, are generally mistrusting, skeptical, vengeful, wrathful, etc. You feel like you found yourself the perfect misfits for lovely little adventure. While the settings are is distant, the voice acting, music themes, dialog, and beautiful portraits of the characters closes the gap. You will grow to like and care for your crew, and you will have to be faced with meaningful decisions regarding them. You have to balance game mechanics over their personality and what you desire. You can see how the wasteland harrows their souls, so do you free them? Or keep them? They will always refer to you to make that decision.  The characters, how the lore works with the characters, were definitely the strongest points of the game.
The Rites:
The gamey game portion of the game. Here you play a sport-like ritutl to get the ball into the enemy's hoop -- I mean pyre. you can use quick and nimble characters to try to score quickly. You can use larger characters with more "prescence" to "tackle" or "tag" adversaries out of the match temporarily.  They did a terrific job in wedging a sport into the lore, like how that banishment after scoring is a metaphorical reminder of your exile.  Because the stakes are high with nearly every match, and because the game continues regardless if you win or lose (you *can* restart, but that breaks the flow and is not necessary in general) I found myself avoiding the use of the experience multipliers that apply handicaps to your team. Compared to Transistor where I used every single multiplier, even with poor weapon combinations, and Bastion where I aggressively used as many as I could. My experience was that while each match was quite stressful (in a good and exciting way), the game was generally easy and I accumulated plenty of experience. I am considering a run where I use as many if not all of the experience multipliers.  Overall, quite fun.
All of the events are considered to be fated by the Stars/Scribes. That said, every character looks to you as for every decision. Ultimately, because of how relatively easy teh game is, you also choose to win or lose each match. What was great about some of the adversaries, is that I seriously considered losing to them on purpose, and if I had that would've still been 'in character'. "Is he not more worthy than my comrade to be saved?" It's great that once again, SuperGiant creates these situations that makes you feel pulled in different directions, without  necessarily forcing you do to so.
The End:
The ending falls short. While there are only 3 different endings, each character can have multiple variatiosn. As a result, are too many permutations, which results in an ending that feels more like a TellTale game that sums your actions and their consequences. I wish there was some sort of cinematic or just a few voice-accompanied images to reallly draw me in and summarize what happened. The End Credit art was unsatisfactory in this regard, especially compared to Bastion. The events that happen are important, large-scale, but they feel like footnotes with how they are conveyed to you.
Other Overall Notes:
-Pacing was excellent. It was not too long where I'd tire of the Rites.
-Music is still superb quality, but felt more in the background and felt less integrated or impactful than Bastion/Transistors. E.g. There is no moment like when Zulf's theme is played. There is no way to interact with the music like humming in Transitor, or the syncing of the game mechanics to the music. This has to do with the fact it's not an actio RPG. Bastion levels were designed to match with the notes and punctuations of the music. That said, the music is used very effectively in mood setting and for character themes.
-Your choices affect the endings. It also affects the lyrics of the ending song. Should you listen to the song all on the album, all of the characters "were true to the end." That line is replaced based on your decisions.

Welp, here is my first review of a game ever. Time to give my honest opinion on The Isle. This will be less of a review and more of a rant on this community and developers.
Gameplay
The game, at this point, has two gamemodes: Sandbox and Progression.
In Sandbox, you pick any animal and play. This gamemode is simple, good, and efficient.
However, Progression is rather crap. Progression works on a basis of points and two "tech trees"; a carnivore and a herbivore one. You gain points by surviving, one per minute. This arises quite a few problems. You can hide in a bush and stay there, only gettting up for food and water. This makes the game just a waiting and almost stationary experience, as you wait 2 hours for a broken carcharodontosaur with a hitbox in its♥♥♥♥♥♥ In fact, Acrocanthosaurus has the same stats as Allosaurus, and they still put this broken animal in the game for an extreme minority of players which have to wait 2 hours for this broken mess! In fact, Acrocanthosaurus is part of a bigger plan I'll outline later.
Community
Is the community bad? Well, I'd say it's pretty evenly split. I have noticed 3 main groups of players. These are:
-the Awesomebros: Their temperament is extremely agressive, often KoSing once they spot a target. They are usually 6-8 year old children. Speech is usually broken. This species' mains vary, most using any variant of Tyrannosaurus, Triceratops or Allosaurus.
-the Carebears aka "XDDDDDDD" types:  Temperament is usually calm, but they are quickly triggered into a blinding rage if they or their comapnions are attacked. These people usually approach other "XDDDDDD" types, to carebear them or be themselves carebeared. Speech usually has copious amounts of emoticons randomly scattered throught usually broken text. Their age range is huge, but a good portion are in their early teens, 12-14 years old. The "XDDDDD" types play almost any animal, favorites for carebears being Tyrannosaurus, Shantungosaurus and Triceratops and the ultimate favorite of the carebeared is the Dryosaurus, who spam the help call, which usually ends in the attacker getting his♥♥♥♥♥whopped by a carebear. Carebears also likely have a small dinosaur OC of which they post pictures on DeviantART.
-the Palaeofans: A group which I am a part of, and this might mean I have a biased view on this group. Temperament is usually calm, collected and strategic. These people only kill for food or for territory, sometimes even enjoying the company of genera that otherwise they would be mortal enemies with. Usually are extinct on public servers and form 100% of the population in realism servers. Age range varies extremely, and I have no idea who are the majority. The variation in mains is absolutely insane.
Developers
Here comes the extremely juicy part. What do I think of the main developers? They rule like dictators above us.
Dondi for example, could be comparable to a tsar, considering himself above us "serfs" and "peasantry". Speaking of Dondi, he is a very arrogant man which does not know how to run a community, constantly mocking us for giving him suggestions. At one point, in April, when the Utahraptor's disease-ridden model was revealed to the world, a great outrage happened, me taking part in it, because of how inaccurate it was. Then, the man snapped and created a secret police made up of moderators, (which I like to compare to the Okhrana, the secret police of the Russian Empire) which silences any opposition.
Dondi is extremely bad at being a buisnessman or a community manager. He has proven this on two occasions:
-the aforementioned one, where he alienated a great part of the fanbase, the palaeofans; which had build up the game and spread its publicity;  by suddenly declaring that the team does not care about accuracy. This crushed support for the game in many circles, including a great promotor, palaeo-Tumblr. The devs lied to us, as we thought we were getting an accurate product.
-removing sandbox. Sandbox is scheduled to be removed, leaving us a depraved waiting simulator for a game, until Progression exits Alpha.
Deathly is again, as bad as Dondi, personally conducting an attack on a server with no KoSing which was about relaxing, Chill Lounge with about 60 people that were to KoS. This attack crushed the server, which only had one moderator at the time, leaving it ravaged.
The devs are scum.
Our Recent Playing By The Devs
The two most recent animals, Utahraptor and Acrocanthosaurus are progression only. This is obviously a ploy to make people abandon the actual good game for the depraved waiting simulator because of natural human curiosity. These devs are obviously not looking to make a good game in which both the customer and the producer are satisfied. In fact, the decisions they have made are so poor, I'm not sure if they even want to make good money. I would not be surprised if this was a cash-grab, like its father, TSL.
Final Verdict
The game is mediocre at best, and it does not seem to be improving. In fact, it seems to be going a dark path.
Can it be saved? Most certainly not, given that the main devs are some of the worst devs I have seen in my whole life. This game is likely doomed.

What a peculiar game.
It's like somebody decided to do a story-heavy basketball game with RPG elements.
What kind of a story? You know, talking dogs, demons, and water-worm knights playing magic basketball to earn their freedom. The obvious choice.
Now, the gameplay is simple and elegant. Textbook example of easy to learn, hard to master. But it's not the main draw of the game. It's actually a very small part, time-wise, and more serves as something to break the monotony. It's diverting, but nothing to write home about.
And there's the one issue with the game; for its price, it's not good gameplay. If you want gameplay, go buy Rocket League.
What this game has, however, is everything else. Aesthetics, story, phenomenal soundtrack, great characters, and lots of immersion. It has so much charm, and so much heart, and it's just so unlike anything else I've ever played that I can't help but love it.
If that's something that interests you, do yourself a favour. Buy this game. Right now. You won't regret it.

So in this section, I'm gonna break it down one by one.
Graphics: 10/10
For a game released in May 2012, this game executed the graphics so well that I thought this game came out in early 2013. The visual aspects of this game is absolutely fantastic, from the beautiful sceneries to the enemy shadows, this game presents really stunning graphics.
Storyline: 6/10
This game has little to no offers when it comes to its 'story'. Despite it being a fun tactical shooter, it has a mediocore storyline. Sound: 8/10
It's a stealth game, so its limited to sound as you need to concentrate with all your might to complete all the missions without getting spotted. Sounds will obviously distract the player. Nonetheless, the sounds from the different weapons, the planes flying by and the enemies were 'satisfying', not Awesome, but still good enough~

Price: 5/10 (dependable on for other people though)
It only gets half the mark for price as it clearly doesnt have any story in the game. If there was a linear story in the game, the price score would be higher, but no...it only gets a 5/10.
Overall, I would highly recommend this game to people who likes stealth and action games.

All the rifles sound the same when they all use different cartridges. I know there were things I noticed about the other weapons, but I can't remember them at this time.
I normally don't find issue with all the incorrect gun stuff in games, but the fact that there are so few weapons and such, makes the flaws stand out that much more and they scream at you constanly.
I think they went about the DLC in a terrible way, but it's not uncommon at this point. I looked at the Sniper Elite 3 DLC situation and was completely disgusted. I assume you only get a couple weapons to choose from and have to buy a dozen DLC packs to get any more. It's just sickening

It'd be great if they did and it allowed you to transfer mobile progress over to the Steam version but nah, that doesn't exist and even if it did, screw you, play through the entire game again, luckily on the Steam version there is cloudsave. The game is basically a 3Dish version of Door Kickers (which I absolutely love btw) but with less freedom in terms of movement, controls, actions, and planning. Its not too bad IMO but its not as great as DK. I think I rated the mobile version as 4 star. Steam version is 2.5 star max. Seriously, don't spend $10.99 on this game. Either get it on sale or buy it on the App Store.
Pros:
- Various Special Forces to choose from all with different stats.
- Weapon customization (at some point during initial release of the mobile version the customization was really good but after a few updates that wasn't really the case).
- You get to choose body armor/uniform. Basically character customization on a fairly basic level.
- Characters Level up individually (i guess that's a good thing?) which allows you to put points into whatever stats you choose for each individual.
- You get to choose what role your characters are (Breacher, Fireteam Leader, etc.)
- The cool top-down to sorta top-down camera switching feature.
- When you watch a replay of your last move you can watch it from the Operator's perspective via over-the-shoulder camera.
-Mobile version requires you to pay real money for "premium" headgear/face accessories. Steam version? Only in-game cash is required.
-CLOUDSAVE! Mobile version doesn't have such a high tech fancy feature. I know first hand.
Cons:
- If you played the mobile version, well obviously no cloud save/transfer as expect so RIP progress.
- Not as much freedom during planning stages
- Something about the character movement doesn't look right to me
- Attachments from initial release (on mobile) have been removed
- Controls aren't that amazing since this is a port of the mobile version.
- THE PRICE! Steam version is flippin' $16.99, meanwhile on mobile it was either $0.99, $1.99, or $3.99. Either way, its cheaper to buy it on mobile.
- It uses a stage-based system if that makes any sense. In DK you can fly through the mission in one swift plan or plan on the go. B&C you get to move a certain distance, and within that distance you plan everything. Once planned, you press the "breach" button and your guys carry on with it. Once they've all moved, you go back to the planning stage and repeat process.
- The amount of "steps" you can take is fairly limited and when you have heavier body armor on, it gets limited even further.
- Once you've chosen a class/role for a character, can't switch. I guess that's a bad thing? It is realistic in the sense that you're trained in that role and that is exclusive to you. You decide weather that's bad or good.
All honesty the game isn't that bad but the Steam version at most is a 2.5 star in my books. Mobile version IMO is 3.5-4 star.

I'm not sure about the label 'platformer' for this game. To me, a platformer game is a much more basic, even simplistic game genre. Yes, Apotheon has a basic platformer layout but the game doesn't consist of jumping from platform to platform, timing each jump carefully to avoid things or to avoid falling to your death. There are only two instances where Apotheon really felt like a platformer but one of those is completely optional (Dionysus) and the other is a very original take on platforming (Athena). If Apotheon is a platformer, it is to modern platformers what 'Gods' was to the SNES and Sega Megadrive (Genesis) consoles. Fun fact: both games are set against a background of ancient Greek mythology, but I digress...
I would rather like to describe Apotheon as a 2D action adventure game with basic roleplaying elements, reminiscent of 'hack and slash' games. The game is mainly about combat. Although not perfect, the combat system in Apotheon is pretty decent. There are several types of weapons, each with advantages and disadvantages (speed, range, damage). You can use a shield to block. There is a stamina bar to make you think about your tactics, as opposed to allow you to just spam the attack button. Weapons degrade over time and break pretty quickly. At first, I didn't like this but soon I came to realize it had two important advantages:
- if you woud be able to use the best weapon throughout the whole game, it would be way too easy and therefore no fun
- this way, you're forced to use different weapons fairly often, making the game more varied and therefore more fun
The story: you are Nikandreos, a warrior whose home town gets destroyed because Zeus (king of the gods) thinks it's time to eradicate humanity because its creation didn't turn out the way he'd have liked. So Hera (queen of the gods) suggests you take up arms and go to Mount Olympus to usurp the powers of each of the main gods, either by proving yourself to them or by defeating them, in order to defeat Zeus. That's it, the whole story of the game.
This is no game you play for its elaborate, deep story. The fun is exploring the realms of the gods, each satisfyingly different enough and each with one or more boss fights, which are mostly well-thought-out and exciting fights.
About the RPG elements:
- there is an extremely limited skill system: you can purchase training for 4 levels of skills for the weapon types (sword, axe, spear, mace, bow)
- more importantly, there are quite a lot of side quests. Even though they are pretty basic (explore, kill or loot), they are varied and interesting enough to pursue. Here I have to specifically mention the Steam Achievements. There is an achievement for each sidequest. This makes doing these quests feel rewarding. Also, you can start from the achievements and see them as a 'quest log' if you want to make sure you don't miss anything.
- there are 'quest hubs' with merchant npcs, with npc houses to explore (and loot!) and with guards who will attack you if they see you you steal or attack anything or anyone.
There is also some crafting of utility items (health potions, armor repair hammers, bombs to throw, ...) to add to the mix. Yes, the art style is 2D and looks very simplistic, but it's actually quite easy on the eye and it fits the game and its settings perfectly. The length of the game is perfect as far as I'm concerned. I estimate it took me about 20 hours and by the time I was about to take on Zeus, even though I was never bored with Apotheon, I felt the game shouldn't go on much longer. All in all, I'm positively surprised by this 'simple platformer' and would certainly recommend it.

I bought the game on the 26th and haven't had any problems with the servers. I know alot of people have given negative reviews here because of that, but I always tend to give games about 5 days after release before I write a review. ♥♥♥♥♥♥ servers are a given with most releases. One thing to consider with this game is that it's developed by a tiny studio, so it'll have more problems compared to most. I follow their twitter and they're extremely responsive to the most minute of problems.
Other than that, the game is amazing. I don't really go for horror games, so this could be given to audiences that tend to get scared easily. The community is very laxed and cooperative, so it brings in team-play very well (Though, you will find your occasional idiot). I really like how the in-game voice chat works. I kept making the mistake of announcing my inventory while Jason was around, so he was able to come up with strategies to counter them. The progression system is pretty slow. I've logged in about 18 hours, and am only level 12 (or maybe that's balanced).
Anywho, the perk system works very well. It adds in to the entertainment of character progression, allowing me to often forget that I still have other things to unlock. Though, I have experienced bugs, but I believe they were fixed during a server maintenance a few days ago.
I play with a controller and have had no problems, except maybe one. It'd be nice if there was a controller mapping option, so I could figure out a place to put the Push-To-Talk hotkey. Honestly, I think it'd be cool if there was a voice-activation feature so we wouldn't need to press the button at all. It is pretty annoying when people have their mic live the entire time.
I'd really like to see different game variants. It does get boring eventually because you know what to expect with minor scenario changes. I think the $40 price tag is a tad bit high because of that, being that there is only one game mode. I don't think single-player would help the price tag much either. Though, if you have friends this game is great. Especially playing with friends who you kinda hate, but not really. You can leave their punkass if you've got a 2-seat car. It feels amazing.
Overall, I give the game an 8/10 considering all of the above. After a month, I'm sure(hope) they will have taken care of mostly everything. I'm excited to see future DLC and fingers crossed for a Jason X skin/map.

A lot of people complaining about the matchmaking. I think a lot of people are just jumping on the bandwagon herer to bash Ubisoft. That isn't to say that the game doesn't have problems though.
PROS:
-The game looks really good. Some of the game modes make it feel like you're in a seige type of battle.
-The controls are spot on and fluid.
-The game has a surprising amount of custumization for a fighting game
-The combat feels substatial. When you hit someone there is a lot of weight behind the sound.
-So far everything I've seen as far as gear and outfits and stuff can be earned without spending any additional cash. It will take a lot of grinding and honestly doesn't affect gameplay (outfits at least).
CONS:
-Matchmaking. It isn't the best. At the time of this review I have less than 20 hours in the game. I have not had any lag issues and there may have been two times that I've been disconnected from a match. It isn't great but it also isn't terrible. It's meh.
-There is a bit of a learning curve and the tutorial is kind of ambiguous on how to perform certain moves. Not a big deal but can be frustrating when you're starting out. Especially since completing the beginner and advanced tutorial gives you steel.
-4v4 modes allow the use of gear. This is really cool but to get the best gear you need to prestige a character to pretige 3 in order to get the best gear. That's really grindy. Thankfully gear doesn't apply to 2v2 or duel modes. So far I haven't been matched with people with max gear.
Final Thoughts:
The game is really fun when it works. A lot of people complain about matchmaking but, while there are some issues, I don't think the problem is as bad as people are claiming. The controls feel great and the mechanics are good. In a technical sense this game is really good. The online experience is a little lacking for a $60 title though. I feel the game is still worth $60 even with the problems it has. I really think they should lower the price to $30 though.

If you miss the days when Rainbow 6 could be played through careful planning and absolutely no effort on your part, then Breach and Clear could be for you.
An immersive, rewarding, and deeply tactical isometric shooter, Breach and Clear lets you hand pick a team to take on the world's threats. And the only threats are, of course, terrorists. But who doesn't love them as bad guys? Psh. Terrorists. What ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s.
Anyway: the game gives you complete control over the movement and actions of your team, allowing you to design the perfect breach and entry, whether it be simultaneous action from two entry points to create a crossfire kill zone, a stacked up door for maximum firepower, or another approach, Breach and Clear gives you those options.
One thing that I also really like: after clearing a level, they replay the fight in real-time, as the game itself is turn-based (sort of.) There's nothing like spending 10 minutes on the perfect run, and then finding out it took all of one minute in real-time. It gives you a lot of respect for those who do this in real life.
10/10, great tactical, turn-based shooter.

Comparing SOMA to Frictional's previous titles I would say it is the least frightening experience they've delivered but the most immersive environment they've created. The story line, location and characters are all interesting and makes you want to keep playing.
The game may be less scary than Amnesia which for me personally may be that I feel more comfortable in a sci-fi setting than in an ancient castle. The environment is great to explore yet it did feel almost lacking in some areas. I felt as though there were a few too many "empty" rooms. Empty meaning the same props you have come across already, no story or puzzle elements, etc.
The voice acting is top notch and really makes you feel attached to the character and the story is the strongest point for SOMA. The thrilling atmosphere is great but I would have loved more puzzles. but don’t get me wrong the game never felt slow, or boring in anyway. You just spend more time exploring this world than doing puzzles. Which I think is new for SOMA coming from Penumbra and Amnesia.
The game is definitely worth picking up and I had great fun playing it.
Technical information
The game is capped at 60fps which can be uncapped.
The game doesn’t natively support SLI but it can be forced with decent performance. I personally experience a lot of texture flickering in out door scenes so I left it off.
Game runs well, I did my play through with a single GTX 670 at 1440p mostly over 60fps.

Before Candy Crush Saga, before all the "match-3" games, there was Bejeweled. (Or Diamond Mine, as it was originally named.)
Bejeweled 3, to me, is PopCap at their best. Masterfully made visuals, music and sound effects combine into a mesmerising, entracing, addicting whole. I can spend hours in the groove, sliding gems into plac, hearing the satisfying clacking and tinkling as they fall on top of each other, setting off chain explosions, planning the perfect hypercube a dozen moves in advance.
Steam says I have 66.9 hrs logged, but I've played this game for hundreds of hours before I ever had it on Steam.
None of the modern free-to-play junk. Here's a full-fledged relaxation game, with several fleshed out modes all based on the simple mechanic of matching gems.
Did I say relaxing? Not all of them are. Some modes leave you with sweaty palms and twitching eyes, searching for that next match, visualising its effect on the whole board, before the timer runs out.
On the other side of the spectrum, you have Zen mode, where you can't lose or run out of time, just accruing more and more points and leveling up, while a talisman gets perpetually crafted with each new level. Seriously, every time I think it can't look any more elaborate the game adds more gems to it. I wonder how far it can go.
This zen endless mode even comes with optional binaural beats and ambient sound (like forest or rain or beach) for maximum relaxation.
Then there's modes like Poker, where you're not on a time limit but you need to think before each move, to get the best hand possible and stay ahead of the increasing restrictions.
Bejeweled 3 falls into the "casual games" genre. And this means a lot of gamers will overlook it or dismiss it as another "game for soccer moms." I mean, it is. But only because it's a game for everyone. It's as casual or as "core" as you want it to be.
(Check my Steam videos for a tiny clip about matching two hypercubes together, a very rare move.)

If you've read the "About the Game" and "Key Features" section, then you have read exactly what the game is. You could say it is the multiplayer title of  S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Be wary, when they say you are fighting for your life, you truly are. This is a survival game, meaning you should not expect to be able to survive an attack of more than 2 or 3 Nether (the monsters in the game) at the same time. Be prepared to be frustrated, and always watch your back. Someone can always be ready to shoot. I have experienced many heart racing shootouts in this game, because you quickly come to realize that death can be a very painful experience.
Talking with many people in-game, a lot agree that the game is good, and it's better than DayZ or Infestation: Survivor Stories. The game is a great concept, and the map is very nice and can take a very long amount of time to actually travel across, as one would expect. The only truly visible errors within the game are the amounts of bugs, glitches, or lag.  However, these are not game breaking, and I expect that they will be fixed, as the developers are releasing more updates. The only thing I can really advise you not to do is walk in the water (however, continually pressing space bar to jump seems to prevent you from drowning and solve the problem) and to not drive the jeep which you will find in the top northwest of the map. Most likely you won't go there anyway.
If you have played S.T.A.L.K.E.R, Metro, or any other similar titles, then Nether is a must-try.
For those who haven't, I still recommend that you play the game if you had even a remote interest in DayZ or other similar titles.

SOMA is a sci-fi survival horror game made by the same studio that gave us Amnesia: The Dark Descent. As a result the two games share quite a lot in common with one another. They are both survival horror games where the player is completely defenseless, and the only way to avoid death is to hide in the shadows from the enemy. They also share completely immersive worlds where each environment in the game can tell you a story based solely off of the objects that populate that specific environment.
However, SOMA, unlike its predecessor puts more of a focus on its story rather than the horror aspects of the game. Normally this would be something that would detract from a horror game, but in this case the story itself is incredibly compelling and wholly unique. SOMA's story is a unique one that focuses on the concept of transhumanism, which is a concept that has been touched on in other games, but not nearly as well as it has here.
Even if you don't care much for horror games, SOMA is a game worth playing through for its story alone.

If I had a choice, I'd give this 'mostly positive.'
I'm a Kickstarter backer but haven't touched the game until recently. It has a steep learning curve, you can make irrecoverable mistakes. I'm on my 3rd game and finally determined a few critical items to build to make long term survival easier.
Sheltered is a deep but simple game about a family trying to survive the apocalypse. You build upgrades, expand your bunker and make tough choices - like whether to take in new followers or turn them away. Send people out to search for supplies, pray for rain, keep your bunker in working order and keep everyone fed, healthy and happy.
RPG elements are fairly light. Stats impact combat, traits give long term bonuses but are offset by a negative trait. Your most important choices are what to spend your precious supplies on. Upgrade your water filter or build a fridge to store food?
I've been enjoying myself, but the gameplay is fairly slow paced. Combat is turn based and usually nothing more than clicking attack or flee.
Negative complaints - very important upgrades may not seem important, nor is much hint given on what you should be building yet. Your people might suggest an upgrade that isn't very important while they starve. Another big one is the interface. With incredibly cumbersome mouse and keyboard controls it's obvious this was designed oddly enough for a controller. It's a game that SHOULD play well with mouse but doesn't. The process of selecting the correct person then giving them the correct command is at times maddening. Even with 16 hours of play it doesn't feel natural.
Overall I recommend this game.

Okay, so the concept of the game is pretty straight forward; You are a biologist with an invested interest in the unknown, hunting a supernatural monster known as the "Rake".
Overral & Single Player Pros:
ONE: More often that not, you'll be jump-scared by the pigs during the day and by the Rake at night.
TWO: The enviroment in which you are hunting the Rake is overabundant with flora (The vegetation), and it is incredibly easy to get lost, especially at night.
THREE: There are certain locations throughout the Rake's World where you can loot extra ammuntion, health packs and weapons, ie, fiearms and bear traps. These locations are tricky to locate, especially in multiplayer as it is night time 24/7.
Multiplayer Pros:
Single player, eeehhh, its fun and all with the jumpscares for the first couple of times, but Multiplayer is much better and funner to play.
ONE: Certain areas of the map during Multiplayer are nonexistent in Single player, which provide extra loot and there's even a tunnel system that passes through the mountain and to another location the Rake haunts, on the other side.
TWO: The more people you can get playing with you, the better the Rake hunting experience will be. For instance, if there's 3+ people playing, one of the three can be the leader as they'll keep their flash light on, whilst the other two turn there's off. You follow the leader into the vegetation and suddenly he turns his flashlight off and runs away (For the sake of mucking around), leaving the two other people by themselves, who turn their flashlights back on and are suddenly attacked by the Rake. I couldn't help myself but do just that.
THREE: You can actrually KILL the Rake! In singleplayer, the amount of ammunition to bring down the Rake isn't plentiful enough through the map, but in Multiplayer, there's more than enough hidden in the Rake's World, you just have to know where to find it.
FOUR: The Rake A.I is ruthless! As soon as I spawned in during a Multiplayer game, I was attacked almost immediatly, that's how unlcuky I was. Later on, my two friends and I were treking our way back to base camp when the Rake was rushing at us, attacking Friend 1, running off as we unloaded on him with our shotguns, then Rake came back, attacked me as Friend 1 was getting his bearings, ran off into the vegetation, came sprinting out several seconds later, attacked Friend 2 as Friend 1 opened fire, before running off. By that time in the game, our health bars were 20% of their original health. The Rake however, had a qaurter health remaining because of similiar occurances earlier on. Later, having remained in the vincinity of our encounter, we set up multiple Bear Traps in a cluster, then fanned out with guns pointing into the nearby vegetation. Although we didn't see him again, we won because he must've ran through the trap we'd set out for him. It was a good match because of teamwork and the fact that we actrually killed the Rake on second crack at him.
HOW DO YOU PLAY MULTIPLAYER?
ONE: Either you have Hamachi which you have to put all the address and port information in yourself, or you can use Evolve which automatically does this for you. I have both, but use Hamachi because I installed it first, and once you've set it up, you stay connected to the server even if not playing Rake. YOU and your FRIEND must both have Hamachi or Evolve to be able to play together.
CONS:
ONE: Playerbase for multiplayer is scarce as you have to convince friends to play with you.
TWO: Visuals aren't the prettiest and the animations are pretty crap.
THREE: No more updates as the Developer lost the Source Code for the game.
FOUR: The player controls have annoying limitations: You cannot jump or crouch, which is frustrating as most games have them.
FIVE: As far as realism goes, the enviroment does not have any affect on your health, ie, you can jump off a cliff edge and fall twenty meters, and have no damage inflicted upon you.
SIX: Multiplayer is not free and you have to set it up yourself through non-steam programs.
OVERRAL:
I recommend this game if you have friend/s who are also actively playing and have either Evolve or Hamachi. This game is not bad, you just have to find others who are willing to play.

This game is far from what is advertised on the steam page now. Unfortunately I am not looking forward to future updates anymore either. The updates are happening such a nonsensical order that it is hard to fathom what the development team is thinking. When I first started playing this game, it was quite playable (other than server crashes) and you could play however you want. If you are new to the game, you will quickly find out that if you don't follow a very strict playstyle however, many of community will try to make your game hell to play. This happens a lot to what the players call "carebears" or players who don't KOS (kill on site) anyone who is the opposite of your diet category. The development team actively has been also trying to eliminate this aspect because they want the game to be as brutal as possible. And that is where the changes have started cropping up and causing issues.
Firstly, new models and such are added regularly, which is great. But they often are released extremely buggy, and loaded with issues. That's fine as well. It is an alpha game, so that is to be expected. The servers used to be sandbox specifically so that those bugs could be quickly found and taken care of. You could play immediately as any dino and developmentally that makes sense. With open access to any dino, all models and interactions with the gameworld would be tested thoroughly by the early access players. An alpha game should frankly have nearly all assests accessible as much as possible for those developmental reasons. But that is no longer the case.
Recently the development team thought it should add the progression type to all servers. This forced all players to queue up into a battle fest of something that should be implemented at the tail end of development, and now it is hindering the testing of the early access community. Logically you would think that all the assets of the game and play would be finished and polished up so that it wouldn't make testing and bug running so impossible. Then after that progression would be implemented. There have been many bugs, and with the continual crashing servers, progression doesn't make sense. You cannot save your progress, and so unless you have pure luck on your side, a ton of time to play the game, and no issues with the game crashing, you might achieve playing as one of the new dinosaurs.
If you have to play for hours to even start to test newly implemented gameplay, you waste so much time on not finding issues that would quickly become prevalent otherwise. For example: The Utahraptor is one of the newer models, but in order to play as it, you have to get through an hour and a half of playing other dinosaurs that have been previously tested and refined. So that is an hour and a half wasted that could be used testing the new dinos and providing constructive feedback. Not many people even have that kind of time to devote to a game, and then on top of that be expected to provide helpful feedback to the development. Thus the logical conclusion is that the progression system will only hinder the game's development at this point and it should be held off from implementation until all the actual gameplay is finalized. I have no problem with progression other than how it is implemented at this point, and that there is no keeping the points for all the hard work a person does in the game. Finally got that T-rex you've been playing for 12 hours to get? Too bad the server is about to crash. Everything gets lost. Progression is not something you throw in when your gameplay isn't even complete. It should be next to last before an official release as it just sets the game up for the actual final product.
But let me advise, providing constructive feedback has only been met by snark and degradation from the development team. Many other players can attest to this, thus I would recommend reading other reviews from the community. The illogical decisions made at this point regarding gameplay, and the way the development team treats their customer-base is so beyond comprehension. For these reasons and more, I cannot recommend this game at this time. Save your money, and hope that things improve farther down the line because the way this is going right now, I cannot see this game being a success.

I'm personally a huge fan of the franchise and like me if you are old enough to have seen back to the future at the cinema you would have been deeply sorrowed when you heard that the entertaining rumours of a back to the future 4 aka back to the future rides again was canned largely because the main actor Michael J Fox had been diagnosed with a debilitating illness known as Parkinsons. With that in mind according to credits it seems that a charity dealing directly with parkinsons benefits from the sales of this game, So with that in mind, how could you ever give this a thumbs down?
The game is a point and click adventure which unlike tell tales other franchises like the 'walking dead', which adds a layer of illusion that your choice matters, here it simply doesn't matter. Instead you just solve puzzles by playing around with things you picked up and placing them at the right place at the right time.
The game continues on 6 months after back to the future 3. The delorean lands back at doc brown residence unmanned with the exception of 'Einstein' doc's dog. (How the delorean survived is explained in one of doc brown's many speech bubbles in game). Marty when he opens up the delorean finds out that the automatic retreival system kicked itself in and that Doc must have got himself into some type of trouble. The only problem is the date system display isnt working properly and Marty has no idea where doc went. The only clue is a womans shoe on the floor of the delorean. From that Marty MUST find out where doc went to and save him.
Because the game storyboard is written by back to the futures original script writer Bob Gale and the voice acting and appearances are from many of the original crew including Christopher Lloyd and Michael J Fox the game plays true and is a fitting tribute to the fluxing back to the future fellow time travellers. There are literally hundreds of easter eggs planted just in the first episode alone which many will miss without a keen eye and a trigger happy screen shot shooter. Also there are MANY speech bubbles with dialogue gems that a impatient person might miss. Take for instance when Tannen is getting his shoes shined. Instead of accepting shining his shoes, decline doing so and then walk up to him again and repeat. His speech changes MANY, MANY TIMES. My personal favorite is, "tell Ma she will get her cut next week!"
The best thing for me is the musical score. I just cant get enough of the music. Amazingly it is even more fitting for a game than it is for a movie. It has the magic of turning a humdrum objective into a 'yeah that's right man I just saved the human race' and on the flip side the other music which has the feel' whoops did i just wipe someone out of existence? My bad!' If god created this world then we have all been jipped. He should have made it so back to the future music follows us everywhere with everything we do. Life would just seem so much more meaningful.
Finishes review with a posted GREAT SCOTT thumbs up!

Not my favorite of SGG games, I don't believe it'll be worth everyone's money and would recommend it sparingly. Given SGG's past success with tidy bundle games of this size, Pyre falls a little short, feeling like the foundation for a great narrative-heavy rpg.
If your goal is to railroad everyone to Liberation, there's not much for you to do.
When I played, the challenge I faced was not wanting to give anyone up to Liberation but begrudging letting (certain) opponents through. I was often in a situation of having to let someone go while yelling "I'm not done with you yet!"
In order to resolve the team's personal stories, you need an amount of world map interactions with them and to have them face certain opponents repeatedly. The struggle lies in the limited number of rites/interactions you get before the next Liberation. Not to mention the world map interactions are how you gather resources or train your team outside of rites, sometimes you might value the benefits of the activites over who you're doing the activity with.
You also get different results depending on whether or not certain characters are [not]Liberated together.
This is further complicated by the fact that battling against certain opponents prompts their banter, but WINNING against them knocks them down and significantly lowers the chance of them reaching Liberation. I found myself planning how to keep down certain teams, encouraging others to success and trying to influence who would meet and when. At times I reluctantly gave up my favorite rite players, people whose stories were unresolved or who may not want Liberation, if the alternative was letting an unrepentant criminal go free.
As an aside, voice acting is great, particularly the Wyrms. There are amazing tiny details; messing with people's stuff in the caravan (Ding ding, dinner's ready! Have a drink or two or five?), bashing into other caravans, running over the wildlife with your caravan. Even surround sound variations in wood density? I love it but what are these priorities.

As of the latest patch, I no longer recommend this game until they fix their problems. Frequent crashes, frequent lag and desync, bad netcode. Over-nerfed and OP weapons, bad matchmaking. Game is becoming more and more of a joke as it gets updated.
***Original Review***
Ok, so is this game worth playing? Yes it is!!!
Does it have problems curently? Yes it does.
Do these problems exist just because it is in beta? No...
So firstly, Survarium is a good game, the concept is  not new, but how many games are? Is it fun, mostly yes. This game has issues though. Now I will defend it in the sense that I feel it is a game worth playing if you like this sort of style, the graphics are grimey, old looking but they fit the mood they are meant to depict in this post-apocolyptic world.
Lag, lag exists in every part of this game from movement to shooting to hit markers. It just lags! Now with me being from South Africa and in general being left out of most game devs minds, I am somewhat used to lag issues, however I even find it annoying and frustrating to play this sometimes. By the way, if you are from South Africa they for some reason decided to region lock the game so you choose a region and are stuck with it. Apparently you can change region once a day but anywhere in Africa is not an option.... Please add a sever in Africa VG!!!
Shooting and hitting an opponent feels like sure luck sometimes.
The leveling system is good, I like the combination between players level, faction level and skill tree. It makes you feel like you are playing towards something.
The weapons are alright, not much to complain about here, yes you can get better guns by paying real money, making this game more pay to win but meh, I'm not too concerned as it's free and fun either way.
JUMPING JUST PLAIN SUCKS. The controls are really, really bad at the moment. Movement feels lethargic and did I mention that the jumping sucks? There is no ability to climb ladders... No ability to go prone... No ability to lean left or right out of cover... As far as controls go this game is basic.. very basic.
Currently the game is having crashing issues at the time I am typing this, however I expected this from a Beta (no matter how much we say games should be in a better state we all know they won't be). What I do like is that when you reconnect it logs you straight back into the game you were playing and you can continue from the exact spot you were when you crashed.
The matchmaking is something I don't like in games (I prefer dedi servers) but with the ability to add friends, create clans (Which are helluva expensive in-game silver) and create squads it so far has not been too bad other than that you occasionaly end up playing with players way above your level and die repeatedly, on the flip side newbies get put in servers with you to and you get to PWN them so yea there's that. This needs to be addressed and fixed though.
SPAWN KILLERS ARE EVERYWHERE!!! The spawn protection that I think currently exists is terrible. There are no repercussion for spawn kiling so players seem somewhat encouraged to do it, it is annoying as♥♥♥♥♥ This also seems to be a thing players need to stop doing, but we know if the opportunity exists to exlpoit a flaw, players will.
All in all, I like this game, I think it's worth playing, and I am hoping the Devs catch a wake up and start patching and improving before the community loses interest and patience in Survarium.

This is one of those games you play when you are just a little too smart for solitaire. While it is a fun game where missions only last a few minutes, it lacks the depth to make it one of those that keep you spellbound.
PROS:
Quick missions that are suited to filling small gaps of time.
Semi-realistic in the urban-combat senario.
Easy to get into without hassling about tutorials.
CONS:
The game becomes repetitive very quickly, so the boredom sets in sooner than with a really good game. The replayability factor is very low.
Every person decides what entertainment is worth in a Dollar amount to them. Bear that in mind in figuring that you'll probably only play this about 3 days out of every year. If that often.
To the uninitiated, this may seem a valuable training-aid in securing hostile urban territory. If that is what you think, it will be less painful to just shoot yourself. No 4-man team will ever insert to clear any but the smallest maps in this game.
This is not the sparkling gem of all games, but it's not the worst out there either. Far more could have been done with the idea, but it seems almost like this game was developed by one guy during a couple of coffee-breaks. It could have been a lot better, though. I hadn't played this game for a couple of years, but I took two squads up to about L20, and now I'm done for the next few years. I also noticed that nothing new was done since I played last, so don't expect new content unless you build it yourself.
While I would reccommend the game, I'd not do it at the $15.00 price tag. Personally, I don't think it should cost even a third of that price, but ultimately, you decide. I think $5.00 is a fair price, and the Frozen Synapse DLC should be thrown in free at that price. Just my $0.02.

It’s hard for me to decide which way to go with this game. On one hand, the early server issues, lack of single player, janky animations and bugs make this a hard sell. Doubly hard when you consider there are only 3 maps and a 40 dollar price tag. But I have had some serious fun with some white-knuckle tense matches, barely surviving as a counselor.  Playing as Jason is enjoyable, but the real satisfaction comes when you see that “You survived” pop up against all odds. Unlike other asymmetrical multiplayer games, it’s possible to have people on your team that totally suck and you still come out on top. There have been a few matches where I’ve escaped by gathering all the parts to a car on my own while my inept peers got murdered around me.
The first time I was driving away with Jason far behind me only for him to step out into the woods in front me did I realize this was definitely an accurate representation of Friday the 13th.
Other examples:
I’ve watched a group of friends playing together get separated and I picked them off one by one as Jason
I’ve run from Jason, thinking I’ve put him behind me, only to have him grab and instantly kill me
I’ve stumbled across the bodies of those trying to get a car repaired – I grabbed all of their parts and managed to get everything repaired while Jason was busy killing on the other side of the map only for Jason to appear at the last moment and murder me
I’ve run upstairs instead of out the back door when Jason showed up
Friday the 13th can be fun, and I have to admit I like it despite almost not wanting to like it when I first started playing. When it goes on sale, I’ll probably try to get my friends to play it.

Completing it took me about 13 hours, enjoyed every bit of it. I don't know about other people, but Machine for Pigs (by Chinese Room, published by Frictional Games, the latter of which made SOMA) gave me a very uniquely flavored emotional experience. I can't describe that sound in my head to you, this otherworldly almost spiritual kind of unique emotional landscape it let me experience. Let's just say there's not just "happiness", "fear", etc. but an infinite landscape of emotional "sounds", and Machine for Pigs zooms in on a very appealing and unique patch of land.
SOMA is a step up from that: The overall emotional cocktail, accentuated by various in-game situations, ultimately gains its taste and impact from the whole package, meaning you need to complete the game to really know what this cocktail tasted like and what it does to you.
Some players will look at various parts of the game and say "Well, it's just this component that I've seen before, and that over there is just that other concept I know, and this kind of story idea has also been done" etc., but they are missing out on the overall experience that, like Machine for Pigs, has its own unique flavor that no other game conveys, plus this flavor is
. Originally, just when I had finished it, my review said "It's the first of its kind. You need to witness it.", that's how strong the experience is.
So, you'll probably realize that some things you hear about and see in the game are not really new - but I hope that you will agree that the way it is put together here and impacts you lets any of those prior similar-ish experiences step into the background.
Sound design is just right, graphics are stellar (especially under water), avatar movement very well done.
The gameplay focuses on story, has some stealth/scares/action, moving through the environment from point A to B plays a central role, and there are some interactions with world objects. The mix works, and if you find something that rubs you the wrong way, try to ignore it and enjoy this creation. The following statement has been overdone, but it's true here: This is a rare gem.

While I believe I'm with the majority of gamers in enjoying the 1st KOTOR the most, I have to say this sequel is very, very good. The story has many layers that continuously peel back to reveal something grander for players to enjoy. The 1st game had players retracing the steps of the antagonist(s); KOTOR II has players trying to hunt down and simultaneously evade multiple antagonists that are very interesting and challenging. Getting to see some familiar faces from the 1st game while enjoying a host of new NPCs and characters, there are no dull conversations or plot points in KOTOR II. Sure the game isn't as polished as its predecessor (due to a rushed release), but it's still highly enjoyable and shouldn't be missed. And thanks to the awesome modders who gave us TSLRCM, we can all enjoy this game again after 14 years in a whole new light...or dark, if you like! Seriously, if you think of yourself as a true Star Wars fan or even just a gamer who loves RPGs, you need to play this game at least once. I know I'm glad I did.

So my feelings on this game are really mixed. Its hard for me to definitely say that I enjoyed the game. I'll go into detail later on how I truly feel about the game. So the story is that you're a pseudo ghost hunter who traveled to San Jacinto to hunt the Rake (a not-so-scary urban creepypasta) and basically you have three days to hunt this creature, while during the day you set up cameras and traps, while you either watch your cameras, defend your camp, or venture into the forest to look for the Rake yourself. Each day the Rake becomes more aggressive, until it decides to launch the assualt on your camp. There is multiplayer (albeit, if you really want to ♥♥♥♥ around, play multiplayer, its complete trash) and normally, a multiplayer mode in a game would make a game better, it didn't. And I'll give the game this: if you are completely blind to what the game offers, then the singleplayer is pretty scary AT FIRST. Eventually you get used to the map, gain some balls, find out that the Rake's model isn't that scary, and the game becomes predictable and boring. The guns do little damage, the Rake does little damage, the fact that medkits can't go in your inventory annoys me, the cameras are basically useless, the jumpscares are just set ways for you to lose health off the bat, and the game is poorly optimized. There are many other reasons the game is trash beyond the ones I've said. Overall, I give the game a solid 5.5/10.Now, you may be asking "Why are you giving the game a thumbs up, when you literally just said the game is horrible.?" The thing is, the game itsself is completly austistic, however, the concept of the game is absolute genius. The idea of being a monster/cryptid hunter and hunting urban legends, cryptids, monsters, and supernatural entities is absolutely gold. Hunting games are rare themselves, as they get boring and are predictable, as deer and wild coyotes arn't that threatening. But hunting something like mothman or the Erlkönig with your friends, all having military equipment is something thats never been done. Basically, what I'm trying to say, is that this ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game actually may have been the first step into a subgenre I like to call "Supernatural Hunting". The game itsself is mediocre, and probably made me lose brain cells, but the actual concept and idea of hunting a supernatural creature (to tie in with lore or story, maybe you're part of an organization such as the CIA or the Vatican) with your friends is great, and I feel like it can actually be explored further, under the guise that it won't be developed by a single Russian programmer who pumped out an abomination like this. I was expecting all my life for a game like this, open world multiplayer (even better if it was mmo but I guess that needs other levels of funding), where you can play as different kind of dinosaurs.
The devs seem to really have a vision and seem to be very hard working as there are updates all the time.
I want to congratulate them for removing the so called "sandbox" style where anyone could pick any species of dinosaur and team up with any kind of dino. This lead to actually having nothing as a goal and 9/10 dinos were TRex. Death was unimportant and all this had a great cost in game immersion.
Now with the progression system they enforced a more natural distribution of species, a realistic ecosystem where the smaller and weaker species in the base of the food chain are numerous and only a few of the top big ones. So now  death matters but its by no means devastating.
I look forward to new updates with new dino species and ages, tribesmen and cannibals (not sure about liking the mercenaries idea though) and ofc the progression system could use some tweaking.
One last thing I d hope to see is if they could make the combat animations (wich are good actually) a little more accurate and synchronized cause right now the fights often are random bites in the air from frenzied running all around dinos, and ofc I d love to see more special animations (right now small raptors can leap on herbs backs, thats nice) like big carnivores mouth grabbing the little dinos and shaking them, throwing them around etc, and hopefully a lot more gore!
Definately recommended, if your into this kind of game, despite the early access.
Keep up the good work devs, you re creating gold here!

I'm following this game as it develops and many things are changed for the better in the last few weeks. This game is vey fun to play if you have friends to play with, but even in single player it can be entertaining.
PROS
BEAUTIFUL GRAPHICS
The landscapes are simply breathtaking and close to photorealistic. The dinosaurs have very fluid movements and a nice soundsset. The dinosaur models are mostly accurate according to the most recent findings (except a few that are lacking feathers).
For this reason, the game is hardware demanding: make sure your PC meets the minimum requirements before purchasing the game.
HUGE MAP TO EXPLORE
The map is nice and very big, this can be both good and bad. If you like to explore like I do, you'll find the exploration part very entertaining. There are a lot of interesting details, human facilities, new lakes and ponds, mountains etc.
UPDATES EVERY DAY
New patches and bugfixes come out every day, on a regular schedule. If after an update the game suffers a catastrophic bug, it is usually fixed after a few hours or maximum a couple of days. The various factions are rebalanced very often to see what works better.
The game is changing and developing very quickly and regularily
CONS
THE COMMUNITY SUCKS
If you like games like Day-Z, this is basically Day-Z with dinosaurs. The community is mostly the same, they are mean, liars, they kill on sight for no reason, they use friendly calls to gain your trust and then murder you... So if you like games like DayZ, go ahead, you'll like this game too, but if you are more chill and like the idea of cooperating in a team then you might be quite disappointed.
YOU CAN'T HOST YOUR OWN SERVER
Devs have recenty removed the ability for players to play single player or host a private server for themselves on the new main map. A new player have NO WAY to learn the map. Many new players complain about dying because not able to find drinkable water, or starving because they keep running in circles and can't find any other player.
BUT I'VE SEEN THIS VIDEO ON YOUTUBE AND IT LOOKS GOOD!
Caution! Many, most videos on youtube (including the trailers in the steam shop) show an outdated version of the game. Puertasaurus is no longer playable now and never will. The skins are different and the map has been completely redrawn now.
Pros:
- beautiful graphics
- very nice sound effects and roars
- fluid animations
- patches and updates come out every day.
cons
- the game is early access so it might have serious issues from time to time.
- the map is not explorable in single player

This is honestly the best game I've played in years. Its too early to really call it (I'm writing this only about an hour after I finished the campaign), but this might be my new favourite game of all time. It's bloody fantastic.
PROS:
- Most obviously, the art. The entire game is gorgeous, start to finish.
- The music. Every track seems to fit the situation perfectly, and a standout few actually brought me to tears.
- The characters. I genuinely cared for many of them, they're all excellently written and almost all of them have actual depth to their personalities. I can think of exactly one whom I didn't feel that way about, and that was likely because I never pursued their subplot. Which leads onto:
- The story. I'll be honest, with most games I tend to look up the ending within a few hours of play. Not this one. I can't imagine how complex this was to write to the point of keeping everything flowing, with subplots and characters evolving or disappearing based on choices, wins and losses. By the end, I was desperately hoping for the game to continue, just a little longer.
- The gameplay. Yes, its basically sportsball. But with 9 classes, actual narrative stakes to every match and AI that can hold its own while still playing fair, its some pretty good sportsball. Though I will note that Normal difficulty felt a bit too easy for me, so I'd suggest sticking it on Hard if you really want to play with the potential to lose and yet continue the story.
The Cons:
- The backstory. It wasn't as compelling as the plotlines in the game and was sometimes difficult to follow, especially early on. You'll have the general gist by the end, but in my opinion the lore was the weakest part of the game. Not bad by any means, but lacking compared to the rest of the game.
- Repetitiveness. The gameplay, while fun, did feel a little samey towards the end. Could have been because I played through about 80% of the game in one sitting, but still.
- Multiplayer is local only. No online play here. Also note that the multiplayer does contain spoilers for the campaign, the game itself will warn you of this.
Note that it is IMPOSSIBLE to get the full story in one playthrough. In fact, to fully resolve every subplot in the game would likely take at least a dozen attempts. Especially since winning matches is what will lock many of them off.
Rating: 10/10

I invited my brother to try this game out one time, and he got a perfect score on his first try.
Me:  "Wow, not bad."
Him:  "I just did what they taught me to do in Infantry School."
So I guess the game works pretty well.
is probably the most fun I've ever had playing a strategy game, largely because its plan-the-next-few-seconds approach both allows the player take his/her time while planning the next move and provides the satisfaction of seeing a successful plan play out in real-time.
Level design is nicely varied while still generally keeping the unwritten rules of play applicable (i.e. the lessons learned from successful/unsuccessful runs of previous missions will be useful in later missions).  I never did figure out exactly what the game used (other than completion speed) to determine the 1-4 star performance rating, but I almost always agreed with the rating it gave me.
the movement and control of squad members is well-thought-out and intuitive.
There is a ludicrously elaborate equipment customization system that I appreciate, and I also like that it unlocks more weapons based on the total number of stars you've acquired as mission ratings.  However, the number of stars required to unlock the guns, as well as the amount of money awarded for missions versus the amount that guns cost, is a bit unreasonable.  Even getting maximum ratings on all of the missions requires several runs through all of the missions in order to have enough stars to unlock the top-tier weapons, and even more runs to get the money to purchase them.  But again, this is a relatively minor complaint, and on the whole the system works well.
In short, while it isn't perfect,
is a solid tactical strategy game with sound core mechanics and enough variety to keep it interesting.  Highly recommended.

Would I recommend Nether? Hmm...
Well, let's take a look at this pitted against a similar game; DayZ Standalone. Both are Survival "Horror" games with zombie-like enemies and features Looting/PvP/Crafting systems on top of it (and we're going to pretend Rust doesn't exist here since its systems are changing as of right now to who knows what..).
Controls?
This one goes to Nether. The movement is incredibly smooth compared to DayZ's choppy/sluggish movement. Also, you can jump in Nether. :3
PvP?
Depending on your play style, this might make you happy or upset. Nether (at least the server I play on) focuses less on PvP and more on PvE. DayZ is pretty much a KOS Fest... Even I get jumpy to the point where if I hear someone else, I will hide on the second story of a building with a Fire Extinguisher raised... and I HATE PvP, even in self-defense.
Looting?
DayZ has useful items in its cities, but is skimpy about it. Nether is very generous with the drops and you won't go hungry if you're brave enough to leave the PvP protection of Safezones to check some abandoned and crumbling buildings. Unlike DayZ though, Nether has a Global Inventory that you can put almost anything in and it will be there for you in every Safezone market even after you die (you can't store cosmetics, but all cosmetics minus the backpacks remain with your character after death if you were wearing them)!
Leveling?
Non-existent in DayZ. Nether has a somewhat okay leveling system based on time spent alive, courier mission successes and how many items you sell, but there’s not a lot to spend the skill points on. The only 3 skills that matter are Guns, Stamina, and Strength; giving bonuses to gun damage, jump height & speed, and extra health/bag room respectively. You only get 1 point in another skill with the level cap being at 31 and each skill being 10 slots. :/
Crafting?
Nether has a very limited crafting system, and the trading doesn't quite make up for it. There also appear to be several recipes for Sniper Rifles, however, even if you have all of the materials, it will not allow you to craft them for some unknown reason. DayZ's crafting system is nice and has a wider variety, though there doesn't seem to be an in-game guide aside from hints in the descriptions and simple Trial-and-Error (and you can’t craft guns).
Enemies?
DayZ's zombies are flippin' unpredictable and glitchy. If a zombie spots you down the street, you better hope to God that you aren't dying of something, because you are going to be running for the next 20 miles if you don't have a loaded gun. These guys sprint just a tiny bit slower than you do, and can snap bones in 1-3 kicks of your shins (I got off lucky twice with 2 kicks each and nothing broke). On top of that, they like to glitch through walls and floors and then un-glitch once inside and proceed to beat you to death.
Nether creatures have a small variety of classes and while they like to twerk on cars and teleport to you, at least you can hit them (and sometimes outrun them)! Circling back to the controls, it's so much easier to hit these guys than the choppy DayZ zombies that I will even take out a Katana against a Tank Nether. A TANK! And I will WIN.
Other Stuff?
The Safezones and courier mini missions are a nice touch in Nether. It makes it feel more like an apocalypse to be running around the city with a few packages while making sure Bandits don’t shank you from behind as a Nether creature beats your face in, plus keeping yourself fed. Oh, and it doesn’t stop there, Chief. Those lovely Safezones I’ve been talking about? They can be attacked and protection will be GONE unless you either repair the Anti-Nether devices around the zone, or you wait an hour for the game to fix it itself.
DayZ has absolutely no safe areas from PvPers and Griefers. You are completely on your own from the start unlike Nether which gives you a small backpack and a kitchen knife that once belonged to a guy named Butter. BUT! DayZ has more detail in its game. Okay, yea, the zombies are bland and OP without a gun as of now, but you can hunt game as of the recent update.
If your friend needs some blood, you can give them some if you have a compatible blood type and the medical supplies (if you aren’t compatible, then they will die horribly from complete system shock and failure as the blood clots up major arteries and you will be ashamed of yourself for making them spawn so far away from you without any defense). Got a can of food you really want to eat that isn’t Sardines? Well I hope you have a can opener or a knife for that. You can use an axe, but that’ll make a mess… Yuck. And don’t forget sickness from cold rain and food poisoning! :D
What does all this mean?!
Welp, it means that both games have their positives and negatives... but ultimately I would not recommend Nether in its current state. Yes, it’s more manageable and appealing for PvPers, but at the end of the day, it’s more like a hiking simulator and the atmosphere isn’t enough to cover this up. The map for its size is actually limited in what the areas REALLY are (you have to pay real life money to unlock half the map), and there isn’t much else to do but loot and deliver packages (or shoot other players for their Butter Knives… you damn griefers you). For what it is, full price is definitely not worth it. $6 is pushing it, but $3 seems to be about right. It's more like a guilty pleasure kind of game that you play for the atmosphere and lolz more than anything else really.
Would I recommend DayZ Standalone at full price? Hell no. Then again, it’s still marked for Early Access, so maybe there is still hope that it will be better than its mod counterpart. Nether is no longer marked as such.

I would recommend this game to all players who like stealth games. This game is definitely worth its price because of its nice graphics and gameplay. This game encourages players to use more of their minds to make new strategies on how to pass a mission and overcome them and because of that it makes finishing a mission much more satisfying.

SOMA is a linear narrative of the philosophical and subjective experience of existence. It deals with metaphysics and the perspectives you have on being by subjecting you through the experiences of a dying patient (the main character and protagonist of the story). Do not expect your choices in this game to really matter outside your own emotional connection to them, there are no "different endings" or real "consequences" but there is a great game here, a very interesting story and an incredibly well-made game in terms of narrative, characters, story and atmosphere. What the game lacks is made up in spades by those elements.
So what does this game lack, you ask? Well, first of all this game is supposed to be a "horror"-experience, and the element is essentially a "monster" walking around in a closed space where you are, and as it comes near you "loud noises" are played followed by different glitches in your "perspective". The rest of the game is essentially, walk from A to B, figure out an easy puzzle and then avoid more of these things, all while solving more easy "puzzles". Once you figure it out the experience can be a bit diluted, but I feel that the story elements and the atmosphere of it definitely make up for it. Personally I'd rather have fewer of the enemies as they just become annoying after awhile. It's not like the gameplay element comes anywhere near the rest of the game... more like a very dumbed down "sneak-game" with contrived puzzles, since the game is so linear, I'd rather have had it be cutscenes and "walking around and looking at the amazing visuals". I do understand that this would almost make the game a "movie" but the gameplay doesn't add anything to the experience in my opinion. Loud music and "jump scare while monster is running at you" over and over just becomes predictably unscary.
With this caveat, this game still has some of the best storytelling I've had in a game lately, and the questions you ask yourself while playing this, while pondering "what's going on" is a rollercoaster unlike any other. Well done!

Back to the Future: The Game is a fine addition to the classic Back to the Future story line. The story starts off fairly straight-forward, but then things get complicated as Marty and Doc go through the adventure. In true likeness to the original movies, nothing is ever simple when it comes to time travel, and simple events create great waves in the timeline.
The gameplay itself is that of a point-and-click adventure, with lots of talking to characters and using items to solve various situations. First, a tip: If you can't join a server, trying hosting your own. Often the problem is that something is permitted in the room you are attempting to join that your client is not setup for.

Only played one multiplayer game. I played as a Gallimimus, a fast little herbivore. There were basically 3 phases: Rush, hectic, and quiet.
First, I found myself racing to find a good source of water. As per the client of the game that corresponds to the timestamp on this review, water is very hard to find for a beginner that hasn't memorized the locations on each map. Then I found myself in a rather quiet phase of the game, only occasionally set upon by predators that had stumbled onto my position, the points which I describe as "hectic." When a predator did find me, it was an exciting chase, despite how easily I would consistently get away.
Of course, this is a single game as the fastest prey in the game. Each dino has its own playstyle, and carnivores look challenging. I will try to update my review when I play more games.
edit: Was trying to update this earlier, but had trouble with my Steam client. Anyway, the previous description was based on sandbox mode, which I found incredibly easy. Progression mode, however, is overwhelmingly difficult. I am not finding a lot inbetween, but until I am up for the challenge I will stick with sandbox on occasion. Really looking forward to how this game turns out. Also fixed up a few typos.

Smarter ones might have realized that with how easy it is for such a giant creature to get stuck when looking for water, all they had to do was scavenge the meat after I died of thirst (which so far seems to just drain the hunger bar faster. Playing as a predator in sandbox mode was pretty easy. Lots of corpses lying around, no need to hunt for myself (I could have if I wanted to, but I decided to just focus on survival).
